The contracts are on [`asyncswap/contracts`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts) `main`. Every
finding of the previous reviews is fixed or acknowledged; see the
[audit scope](/audit/scope). These docs rebuild from that repository on every change to its
sources, guides or audit notes.

# Async Swap protocol

Async Swap is a Uniswap v4 hook that turns exact-input swaps into resting limit orders. The hook uses v4
custom accounting (`beforeSwapReturnDelta`) to take the whole swap input as an order, and v4 flash accounting
(one `PoolManager.unlock` per action, every delta zero at the end) to settle matches, fills and fees. Orders
are good till cancelled (GTC): there is no expiry, so an order rests until it fills or the maker cancels it.

This page is the entry point. It shows the contracts, where funds sit, how an order is placed, and who may do
what. Every box names a contract, library or function in `src/`, so the diagrams can be checked against the code.

## Guides

| Guide | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Order lifecycle and priority bids](/protocol/order-lifecycle) | Create, match, reprice, top up, cancel; bid settlement |
| [Flash fills and non-numeraire pools](/protocol/flash-fills) | `fillOrderWithCallback`, nested `fillOrderInCallback`, the per-fill MEV tax, pools without USDC |
| [Dutch auction orders](/protocol/dutch-auction) | `startAuction`, steps, fills |
| [Contract call sequences](/protocol/contract-call-sequences) | Step-by-step calls for placement, fills, cancels, setup and withdrawals |
| [Priority fee top-ups](/protocol/priority-fee-top-ups) | `topUpPriorityFee` and agent batching |
| [Signed price changes](/protocol/repricing-signatures) | `UpdatePrice` and `CancelOrder` typed data |
| [Price keys and crossing](/protocol/price-key-crossing) | How limit prices become v4 tick keys and when two orders cross |
| [Dynamic fee ordering](/protocol/dynamic-fee-ordering) | How pool-fill backruns pay LPs and the protocol |
| [Deployments](/deployments) | Addresses per chain |

## 1. Components

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Actors
        Maker["Maker"]
        Relayer["Relayer<br/>(signed orders, cancels)"]
        Filler["Filler<br/>(EOA or flash-filler contract)"]
        Anyone["Anyone<br/>(matchBook, fillFromPoolLiquidity,<br/>stepAuction, pool setup)"]
        LP["v4 LP"]
        Owner["Protocol owner"]
    end

    subgraph Periphery
        Router["Router<br/>swap · swapWithSig · fillOrder<br/>cancelOrder · cancelWithSig · cancelAndWithdraw<br/>withdrawClaims · topUpPriorityFee<br/>matchBook · fillFromPoolLiquidity · multicall<br/>mevTax"]
        RFF["RouterFlashFills<br/>fillOrderWithCallback · fillOrderInCallback<br/>matchBookInCallback · mevTaxFor · mevTaxOwed"]
        Base["AsyncSwapFlashFiller<br/>abstract base: write _route"]
        Permit2["Permit2"]
        Claims["NativeClaims · TokenClaims"]
    end

    subgraph Core
        PM["Uniswap v4 PoolManager<br/>unlock · swap · ERC-6909 claims"]
        Hook["AsyncSwap hook<br/>beforeInitialize · beforeSwap · beforeAddLiquidity<br/>matchNewOrder · executeOrder · flashFill<br/>updatePrice(WithSig) · startAuction · stepAuction<br/>cancelOrder · matchBook · tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity"]
        Libs["Linked libraries<br/>(see section 5)"]
        Vault["FeeVault<br/>collect(currency, recipient)"]
    end

    Maker -->|orders, cancels, claims| Router
    Maker -->|setExecutor, updatePrice, startAuction| Hook
    Relayer -->|swapWithSig, cancelWithSig| Router
    Relayer -->|updatePriceWithSig| Hook
    Filler -->|fillOrder| Router
    Filler -->|fill| Base
    Base -->|fillOrderWithCallback| Router
    Router -.->|fallback: DELEGATECALL| RFF
    Anyone -->|matchBook, fillFromPoolLiquidity| Router
    Anyone -->|stepAuction| Hook
    LP -->|modifyLiquidity| PM
    Owner -->|collect| Vault

    Router -->|unlock| PM
    Router -->|signed input| Permit2
    PM -->|beforeSwap| Hook
    Router -->|hook entry points| Hook
    Hook -.->|DELEGATECALL| Libs
    Hook -->|take · mint · burn · settle · swap| PM
    Vault -->|burn + take| PM
    Maker -->|redeem| Claims
    Claims -->|burn + take| PM
```

Anyone may open a pool on the hook with the dynamic-fee flag. A pool that holds the chain's USDC (`numeraire`)
opens freely. A pool without it, such as ETH/TOKEN, opens once both tokens already have a numeraire pool on this
hook with the same tick spacing; see [non-numeraire pools](/protocol/flash-fills#non-numeraire-pools).

Each order must meet two floors, fixed when the pool opens:

* **Minimum order** on the quote leg: USDC on a numeraire pool, from the constructor's whole-dollar
  minimum scaled by `decimals()`.
* **Asset floor** on the other leg: `10^(decimals - assetPrecision)` base units (0.0001 token with the
  deployed precision of 4). Native ETH counts as 18 decimals; an asset with no code is rejected.

No check reads a price, and nothing has a setter, so the owner cannot change the rules under live orders.
`beforeAddLiquidity` is a pass-through: ordinary v4 range positions are the inventory for pool fills. No user
swap reaches the AMM curve directly, because `beforeSwap` takes the whole input as an order. The standalone
`MatchingEngine.sol` is a benchmark harness and is not deployed.

## 2. Where funds live

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph PoolManager["PoolManager (custody)"]
        Escrow["Hook claims<br/>= open orders' remaining input<br/>+ escrowed priority bids"]
        Fees["FeeVault claims<br/>trade fees · pool-fill fees<br/>half of each dynamic fee<br/>settled bids · MEV tax (native)"]
        User["Maker and filler claims<br/>match proceeds, refunds,<br/>native payouts, flash-fill input"]
        Reserves["Pool reserves<br/>v4 LP positions"]
    end
    MakerW["Maker wallet"] -->|input on swap| Escrow
    Escrow -->|cancel| MakerW
    Escrow -->|book match| User
    Escrow -->|filler fill| FillerW["Filler wallet"]
    Escrow -->|flash fill: input as claims| User
    FillerW -->|fill: output| MakerW
    Escrow -->|fees, bids| Fees
    Reserves -->|pool fill output| MakerW
    Reserves -->|dynamic fee: half| Fees
    Fees -->|collect| OwnerW["Owner-chosen recipient"]
    User -->|TokenClaims / NativeClaims /<br/>Router.withdrawClaims| MakerW
```

| Fee | Rate | Paid by | Event |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trade fee, book match or filler fill (plain or flash) | 0.02% of what each side receives, rounded up | both sides | `OrderFeeAccrued`, one per side |
| Protocol fee, pool fill | 0.01% of the input swapped | the order | `OrderFeeAccrued` |
| LP fee, pool fill | 0.02% dynamic LP fee | the order | PoolManager `Swap` |
| Dynamic fee, pool fill that backruns | half the price gap it closes | the order, in its output | `DynamicFeeCharged` |
| Priority bid | maker's choice, USDC, non-refundable | the maker | settles with fills and closes |
| MEV tax | priority fee per gas × `MEV_TAX_GAS`, in ETH | the transaction, per order creation or fill | Router `MevTaxPaid(payer, amount)` |

`calculatePoolFee` and `calculateHookFee` are zero. A maker's guarantee is its minimum output minus 0.02%.
Refunds and cancels are not charged. See [dynamic fee ordering](/protocol/dynamic-fee-ordering) for the pool-fill fee.

**MEV tax.** The Router charges `mevTax()` on `swap`, `swapWithSig`, `fillOrder` and `fillFromPoolLiquidity`,
and on every flash fill (the outer fill and each nested `fillOrderInCallback`). On a chain that orders
transactions by priority fee, searchers racing for one position bid that fee up, and the tax turns most of the
bid into protocol revenue. A transaction with no priority fee pays nothing. Plain actions pay it in `msg.value`;
flash fills pay it in flash-accounting style, see [paying the MEV tax](/protocol/flash-fills#paying-the-mev-tax).
Cancels, claims, top-ups, `matchBook` and `stepAuction` are not taxed. A searcher can still race untaxed by
repricing its own order and settling it with `matchBook`; no user loses funds that way, the protocol only
collects less (acknowledged in the 2026-11-01 Pashov review, findings 4, 5, 6 and 9).

**Invariant.** The hook's claim balance per currency equals the remaining input of open orders plus escrowed
bids, fuzzed by the matching invariant suites. The hook's own token balance is zero between transactions, so
`sweep` only moves funds sent to the hook by mistake.

## 3. Placing an order

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant M as Maker
    participant R as Router
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant H as AsyncSwap hook
    participant IM as IncomingMatching

    M->>H: setExecutor(poolId, Router, true), once per pool
    M->>R: swap(order, userData) + MEV tax in msg.value
    R->>PM: unlock(Swap)
    PM->>R: unlockCallback
    R->>PM: settle MEV tax, mint it to FeeVault as native claims
    R->>PM: swap(key, exact input, hookData)
    PM->>H: beforeSwap(sender = Router)
    H->>PM: take input as hook claims
    H->>IM: stage(order): check floors, escrow bid
    Note over H,IM: A crossing arrival with no active LP liquidity<br/>is staged in transient storage, otherwise stored in the book
    H-->>PM: BeforeSwapDelta takes the whole input (custom accounting)
    R->>PM: settle input (transferFrom, ETH, or Permit2)
    opt priorityFee > 0
        R->>PM: settleFor(hook) with the USDC bid
    end
    R->>H: matchNewOrder(order)
    H->>IM: better venue first: pool or book, up to 8 pairs
    opt Remainder and active liquidity
        H->>H: guarded self-call fillOrderFromPoolLiquidity
    end
    H-->>R: matched pair count
    R-->>PM: callback returns, every delta is zero
```

Signed orders follow the same path through `swapWithSig`: one Permit2 `PermitWitnessTransferFrom` whose witness
is `OrderSignatures.hashOrder(order)`, plus an optional signed `SetExecutor` grant. An order's id is
`keccak(chainId, poolId, owner, zeroForOne, salt)`; the hook assigns the salt and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated`.

The new order goes to the better venue first. If the pool has active liquidity and its spot price is strictly
better than the best opposing level, the pool fills up to that level and the book takes the rest. Otherwise
the book matches first and the pool must take the whole remainder or roll back. See the
[lifecycle](/protocol/order-lifecycle) for everything after placement.

## 4. Authorization

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph MakerRights["Maker (order.owner)"]
        m1["Router: swap, cancelOrder, cancelAndWithdraw,<br/>withdrawClaims, topUpPriorityFee"]
        m2["Hook: updatePrice, startAuction,<br/>setExecutor, invalidateNonce"]
        m3["Signatures: Permit2 order witness,<br/>SetExecutor, UpdatePrice, CancelOrder"]
    end
    subgraph RouterRights["Router (trusted, fixed in the hook)"]
        r1["only swap caller beforeSwap accepts"]
        r2["executeOrder, tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity:<br/>needs the maker's executor grant"]
        r3["flashFill: Router only, needs the grant"]
        r4["cancelOrder and topUpPriorityFee:<br/>Router only acts for order.owner"]
    end
    subgraph FlashRights["Active flash filler"]
        f1["fillOrderInCallback, matchBookInCallback:<br/>only msg.sender in the transient filler slot"]
    end
    subgraph OwnerRights["Protocol owner (two-step transfer)"]
        o1["FeeVault.collect"]
        o2["sweep: hook's raw balance only"]
        o3["no pause, no upgrade, no setter, no escrow access"]
    end
    subgraph Public["Anyone"]
        p1["open a pool"]
        p2["matchBook(key, 1..8)"]
        p3["fillFromPoolLiquidity(order)"]
        p4["fillOrder / fillOrderWithCallback (pays the maker)"]
        p5["stepAuction(order)"]
        p6["relay a maker's signature"]
    end
```

`Router.multicall` runs several Router calls atomically as the caller. It is not payable, so native-value
actions are sent on their own. The Router can never be revoked as an executor (`CannotRevokeTrustedRouter`), so
a maker's orders are never trapped. Signed maker actions use unordered nonces in `AsyncSwap.nonceUsed`;
`invalidateNonce` revokes any of them.

## 5. Modules and libraries

Measured with solc, the hook and Router sit near the EIP-170 limit, so most logic runs in linked libraries and one
Router module. Public library functions run by DELEGATECALL in the hook's context, so escrow, books and transient
records stay in the hook.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph RouterSide["Router side"]
        Router["Router"]
        RFF["RouterFlashFills<br/>created in the Router's constructor"]
        Router -.->|"fallback() and FlashFill unlock:<br/>DELEGATECALL, runs as the Router"| RFF
    end

    subgraph HookSide["AsyncSwap hook + linked libraries"]
        Hook["AsyncSwap"]
        IM["IncomingMatching<br/>stage · matchNewOrder · venue choice"]
        AM["AsyncMatching<br/>matchBook · fill · cancel · updatePrice<br/>fillFromPoolLiquidity"]
        MA["MultiAsset<br/>initialize (pool setup) · run (flashFill ops)"]
        DA["DutchAuction<br/>start · step"]
        PFU["PriorityFeeUpdates<br/>topUp"]
        DFO["DynamicFeeOrdering<br/>charge"]
        TP["TickPrice<br/>limit price to tick key"]
        TB["TickBitmap"]
        EP["EligiblePrice"]
        AF["AsyncFiller (internal)<br/>State, Book, fees, bids"]

        Hook -.->|linked| IM
        Hook -.->|linked| AM
        Hook -.->|linked| MA
        Hook -.->|linked| DA
        Hook -.->|linked| PFU
        IM -.->|linked| AM
        AM -.->|linked| DFO
        AM -.->|linked| TP
        AM -.->|linked| TB
        AM -.->|linked| EP
        MA -.->|linked| EP
        PFU -.->|linked| EP
        DA -.->|linked| TP
        DA -.->|linked| EP
        AM --> AF
        MA --> AF
        DA --> AF
    end

    Router -->|calls| Hook
    RFF -->|"flashFill(op), stepAuction,<br/>asyncOrderInfo, matchBook"| Hook
```

`RouterFlashFills` called directly reaches the hook as itself, not as the Router, and `flashFill` refuses it
(`NotTrustedRouter`). Its code counts toward the Router's initcode, not its runtime.

## 6. Deployment shape

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["CREATE2 deployer"] -->|fixed salts, same address on every chain| Libs["TickPrice · DynamicFeeOrdering · TickBitmap<br/>EligiblePrice · PriorityFeeUpdates · MultiAsset<br/>DutchAuction · AsyncMatching · IncomingMatching"]
    Libs -.->|linked into bytecode| Hook["AsyncSwap hook<br/>mined salt for the hook flags"]
    D --> Hook
    Hook -->|constructor| Vault["FeeVault"]
    Owner["Deployer"] -->|CREATE| Router["Router(PoolManager, hook, Permit2, MEV_TAX_GAS)"]
    Router -->|constructor: new| RFF["RouterFlashFills"]
    Owner -->|CREATE| Claims["NativeClaims · TokenClaims"]
    Anyone["Anyone"] -->|PoolManager.initialize| Pool["Pool: dynamic fee, hook address"]
```

`script/deploy.sh <chain-key> [dry-run|broadcast|verify]` runs this sequence from `script/config/chains.json`.
`MEV_TAX_GAS` comes from the chain's `deployment.mevTaxGas`: 20,000,000 on Unichain, whose blocks are ordered by
priority fee, and 0 on chains ordered another way, where it would only tax ordinary tips. Measure contract
sizes with `forge build && python3 script/check-contract-sizes.py`.

# Order lifecycle and priority bids

Orders are good till cancelled (GTC). The order struct has no expiry, and nothing closes an order on a timer: it
rests until it is fully filled or the maker cancels it. A signed message (`swapWithSig`, `updatePriceWithSig`,
`cancelWithSig`) carries a `deadline`, but that only limits when the signature can be submitted.

See the [protocol overview](/protocol/overview) for the contracts and the [call sequences](/protocol/contract-call-sequences)
for each step as calls.

## States

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Open: swap / swapWithSig
    Open --> Open: partial book match or pool fill up to a book level
    Open --> Open: reprice (updatePrice, updatePriceWithSig)
    Open --> Open: topUpPriorityFee
    Open --> Auction: startAuction (maker)
    Auction --> Auction: stepAuction writes the scheduled minimum
    Auction --> Open: maker reprice, or schedule reaches its floor
    Auction --> Closed: any fill, match to zero, or cancel
    Open --> Closed: filled in full
    Open --> Closed: remainder below the pool minimum
    Open --> Closed: cancel
    Open --> Closed: flash fill (closed before the filler callback)
    Closed --> [*]
```

A closed order is deleted. Its remaining bid settles to the FeeVault and any unused input returns to the maker.

## Lifecycle

Book matching ranks the best opposing price first; a higher escrowed USDC bid breaks ties at one price, then
earlier submission. Filler fills, flash fills and pool-fill retries target one order and do not follow the book's
queue.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Router.swap / swapWithSig<br/>input, minimum output, optional USDC bid, MEV tax"] --> B["beforeSwap takes the input (custom accounting)<br/>check quote minimum and asset floor<br/>escrow input and any bid"]
    B --> V{"Active liquidity and pool spot price<br/>strictly better than the best opposing level?"}
    V -- "No" --> F["Book first: match up to 8 crossing pairs"]
    V -- "Yes" --> PF["Pool first, limited at the best opposing level"]
    PF -- "Filled" --> Z["Closed"]
    PF -- "Stopped at the level, or reverted" --> F
    F --> I{"Still open?"}
    I -- "No" --> Z
    I -- "Yes" --> J["Try the remainder against pool liquidity"]
    J -- "Filled" --> Z
    J -- "Rolled back" --> R["Resting order"]

    R -- "New crossing order or Router.matchBook" --> N["Bounded book matching"]
    N -- "Remainder" --> R
    N -- "Done, or remainder below minimum" --> Z
    R -- "Router.fillFromPoolLiquidity" --> J
    R -- "Router.fillOrder" --> O["Filler pays the live minimum<br/>if it is within maxPrice"]
    O --> Z
    R -- "Router.fillOrderWithCallback<br/>or fillOrderInCallback" --> FL["Flash fill: see flash-fills.md"]
    FL --> Z
    R -- "topUpPriorityFee" --> T["Fund extra bid; back of the new fee tier"]
    T --> R
    R -- "updatePrice" --> Q["New minimum; fresh time priority"]
    Q --> R
    R -- "startAuction / stepAuction" --> DA["Minimum falls on a schedule: see dutch-auction.md"]
    DA --> R
    R -- "cancelOrder / cancelWithSig / cancelAndWithdraw" --> C["Return remaining input; settle remaining bid"]
    C --> Z
```

Notes:

* `updatePrice` only re-ranks the order. It needs no unlock and triggers no matching; a later crossing order,
  `matchBook`, a filler or a pool-fill retry executes it. Each reprice increments `orderReprices`, which voids
  older signed reprices.
* `Router.matchBook` accepts 1 to 8 pairs and does not retry pool liquidity. `matchBook` skips a pool while a
  new order on it is still being funded.
* A crossing arrival on a pool with no active LP liquidity is staged in transient storage by `IncomingMatching`
  while it is funded, matched in memory against the book, and only its remainder is stored.
* Book-match proceeds and refunds below the pool minimum are paid as PoolManager claims, so a token that refuses
  a recipient cannot block matching. Filler and pool fills pay ERC-20 output directly; native output is paid as
  claims (id 0). Flash fills pay the filler in claims.
* Holders redeem claims through `TokenClaims`, `NativeClaims` or `Router.withdrawClaims`.
  `Router.cancelAndWithdraw` cancels and withdraws native input in one step.

Sources: [Router](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/Router.sol), [AsyncSwap](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/AsyncSwap.sol),
[IncomingMatching](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/IncomingMatching.sol), [AsyncMatching](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol),
[AsyncFiller](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol).

## Priority bids

Bids are optional and paid in USDC, so only numeraire pools accept them. A zero-bid order pays nothing and keeps
time priority among zero-bid orders. A nonzero bid is escrowed and **non-refundable**; it must be at least
`min(0.10 USDC, 0.1% of the order's USDC notional)`. Bids rank same-price orders in the book; they do not buy
block inclusion. The chain's priority fee is a different thing: the Router taxes it (the MEV tax, see the
[overview](/protocol/overview#2-where-funds-live)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Bid escrowed as hook claims"] --> B{"Order event"}
    B -- "Book match, or pool fill up to a book level" --> C["Settle the filled share:<br/>floor(remainingBid * inputUsed / remainingInput)"]
    C --> D{"Remainder meets the pool minimum?"}
    D -- "Yes" --> E["Keep the rest escrowed; re-rank"]
    E --> B
    D -- "No" --> F["Settle all remaining bid; close"]
    B -- "Filler, flash or pool fill in full" --> F
    B -- "Cancel" --> F
    B -- "Reprice or auction step" --> E
    B -- "Top-up" --> E
    C --> K["Bid claims to FeeVault, in the same unlock"]
    F --> K
```

Bids always go to the FeeVault, never to LPs, so liquidity added just before a settlement earns none of them. A
failed pool-fill self-call rolls back its fee and bid changes and keeps earlier book matches.

Raising a sell's minimum output requires a nonzero remaining bid to meet the new notional's bid floor. A
partially filled order keeps its prorated bid when repriced to unchanged or lower terms. Sources:
[`_reduceAfterMatch` and `_settleMatchedPriorityFee`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol),
[`settlePriorityFee`, `fill` and `cancel`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol).

## Top-ups, cancels and withdrawals

* `Router.topUpPriorityFee(order, addedFee)` funds a larger bid. The order joins the back of its new fee tier;
  its input, limit price and maker age stay the same. See [priority fee top-ups](/protocol/priority-fee-top-ups).
* `Router.cancelAndWithdraw(order)` cancels and sends native input straight to the maker's wallet, given an
  exact claim allowance for id 0. ERC-20 cancels already return tokens.
* `Router.withdrawClaims(currencies, amounts)` redeems up to 16 currencies of the caller's own claims.
* `Router.multicall(calls)` batches any of these atomically, each as the caller.

# Flash fills and non-numeraire pools

A flash fill lets a filler fill an order with no inventory. The Router gives the filler the order's escrowed input
first, as ERC-6909 claims, calls the filler back inside its own `PoolManager.unlock`, and only then collects the
maker's output. Inside the callback the filler can swap on any Uniswap v4 pool, fill other Async Swap orders with
`fillOrderInCallback`, and run `matchBookInCallback`, in a loop it controls. This is v4 flash accounting: nothing
has to be funded up front, as long as every delta is zero when the unlock ends.

## Interfaces

* `IAsyncSwapCallback`, served by the Router: `fillOrderWithCallback` opens a fill; `fillOrderInCallback` and
  `matchBookInCallback` work only while that callback runs, and only for its filler; `mevTaxFor` and
  `mevTaxOwed` price the tax.
* `IAsyncSwapFlashFiller`, implemented by the filler: `asyncSwapFlashFill(order, amountIn, amountOwed, data)`.
* `AsyncSwapFlashFiller` (`src/periphery`): an abstract base that implements the callback. Inherit it and write
  `_route`.

The Router serves `IAsyncSwapCallback` from `RouterFlashFills`, a module it creates in its constructor and runs by
DELEGATECALL from its `fallback`, so every call runs as the Router. The Router's `unlockCallback` forwards a
`FlashFill` unlock to the same module. On the hook side, `AsyncSwap.flashFill(args)` is Router only and runs three
ops in the linked `MultiAsset` library: 0 begin, 1 settle, 2 fill paid in claims.

## Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Owner as Filler owner
    participant F as Filler (AsyncSwapFlashFiller)
    participant R as Router + RouterFlashFills
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant H as AsyncSwap hook
    participant MA as MultiAsset
    participant V4 as Any v4 pool

    Owner->>F: fill(order, maxPrice, data)
    F->>R: fillOrderWithCallback(order, maxPrice, data)
    R->>PM: unlock(FlashFill)
    PM->>R: unlockCallback, forwarded to RouterFlashFills
    R->>H: stepAuction(order), then asyncOrderInfo
    Note over R: live minimum within maxPrice,<br/>live input at least order.amountIn
    R->>PM: mint MEV tax to FeeVault (Router now owes ETH)
    R->>H: flashFill(op 0 begin)
    H->>MA: run: close the order, settle its bid,<br/>credit input less 0.02% to the filler as claims
    R->>R: tstore filler slot
    R->>F: asyncSwapFlashFill(order, amountIn, amountOwed, data)
    rect rgba(128, 128, 128, 0.12)
        Note over F,V4: _route: any mix, any order
        F->>PM: burn claims, swap, take, settle, mint
        PM->>V4: swap
        loop Nested fills
            F->>R: fillOrderInCallback(other, maxPrice)
            R->>H: stepAuction, asyncOrderInfo, check maxPrice
            R->>PM: mint MEV tax to FeeVault (Router owes more)
            R->>PM: transferFrom(filler, hook, other's output claims)
            R->>H: flashFill(op 2 fill)
            H->>MA: pay its maker, credit its input less 0.02% to the filler as claims
        end
        opt Continue a crossed book
            F->>R: matchBookInCallback(key, maxMatches)
            R->>H: matchBook
        end
        F->>PM: approve(Router, output id, amountOwed)
        F->>R: mevTaxOwed()
        F->>PM: sync(ETH), settleFor(Router) with the tax owed
    end
    R->>R: clear filler slot
    R->>PM: transferFrom(filler, hook, amountOwed output claims)
    R->>H: flashFill(op 1 settle)
    H->>MA: pay the maker its minimum less 0.02%
    R->>PM: settle any prepaid msg.value, check the Router's ETH delta
    Note over R,PM: delta < 0 reverts MevTaxUnpaid(owed),<br/>delta > 0 is taken back to the filler
    R-->>PM: callback returns, unlock ends only if every delta is zero
```

Every payment inside a flash fill is a claim: the order's input is credited to the filler as claims, a nested
fill pulls its output from the filler as claims (`transferFrom`, so the filler approves the Router per currency),
and the final maker check pulls the owed output as claims. A route that only moves between Async Swap books never
opens a PoolManager delta at all. Swaps on other v4 pools are bridged with `burn` (claims to credit) and `mint`
(credit to claims). Native ETH is claim id 0.

The maker of the outer order is paid as in a plain fill: ERC-20 output as tokens, native output as claims. Any
surplus above `amountOwed` stays with the filler.

## Paying the MEV tax

Each flash fill owes the MEV tax once per fill: the outer fill and every `fillOrderInCallback`.
`matchBookInCallback` pays none, as `matchBook` is open to anyone anyway. The tax is paid flash-accounting style:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Each fill:<br/>Router mints the tax to FeeVault<br/>as native claims"] --> B["Router's ETH delta<br/>goes negative by the tax"]
    B --> C{"Who pays?"}
    C -- "msg.value on fillOrderWithCallback" --> D["Router settles the prepayment<br/>after the callback"]
    C -- "In the callback" --> E["Filler: sync(ETH),<br/>settleFor{value: mevTaxOwed()}(Router)"]
    D --> G{"Router's ETH delta"}
    E --> G
    G -- "below zero" --> X["revert MevTaxUnpaid(owed)"]
    G -- "zero" --> OK["unlock closes"]
    G -- "above zero" --> S["take the surplus to the filler"]
```

* Off chain, `mevTaxFor(fills)` quotes the tax for `fills` fills. Call it with the gas price you will send
  (`eth_call` with `gasPrice`, or `forge script --with-gas-price`).
* Inside the callback, `mevTaxOwed()` returns exactly what the Router still owes: every fill charged so far
  less what was paid.
* With no priority fee the tax is zero.

`AsyncSwapFlashFiller` pays `mevTaxOwed()` from its own ETH balance at the end of the callback.
`ethNeeded(fills)` tells the owner how much ETH to send with `fill`, and `script/FlashFill.s.sol` sends exactly
that. `withdraw` returns surplus ETH and claims to the owner.

## Safety rules

| Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|
| The flash-filled order cannot be repriced, cancelled, topped up, matched or filled again during the callback. | Op 0 deletes it before the callback; later calls find `OrderNotFound`. |
| No other Router entry point runs during the callback. | Each opens its own `unlock`, which v4 refuses (`AlreadyUnlocked`). A nested `fillOrderWithCallback` reverts `FlashFillActive`. |
| Only the active filler may use the in-callback entry points. | `onlyFlashFiller` reads the transient filler slot, cleared before the output is collected. |
| The maker check is on the final amount only. | The owed output is pulled once, after the callback. |
| Resting orders filled inside a flash fill are never worse off. | `fillOrderInCallback` applies the same live minimum, `maxPrice`, `order.amountIn` bound and 0.02% fees as `fillOrder`. |
| Dutch auction orders fill at the scheduled price. | Both entry points call `stepAuction` before reading the price. |
| Only the Router drives the hook side. | `flashFill` reverts `NotTrustedRouter` for any other caller and checks the maker's executor grant. Op 1 only settles the order op 0 opened in the same transaction (transient record in the hook). |

## Non-numeraire pools

A maker can place an order on a pool without the numeraire, for example ETH/TOKEN. Fillers fill it like any
order, and a flash fill routes it through the two numeraire books with no inventory: sell into one book, buy from
the other, and the USDC in the middle nets to zero inside the PoolManager.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    O["Order on ETH/TOKEN<br/>sells ETH for TOKEN"] -->|"op 0: ETH claims to filler"| F["Flash filler"]
    F -->|"fillOrderInCallback:<br/>pay ETH, get USDC"| B1["ETH/USDC book"]
    F -->|"fillOrderInCallback:<br/>pay USDC, get TOKEN"| B2["TOKEN/USDC book"]
    F -->|"op 1: TOKEN claims to the maker"| O
```

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Who may open one | Anyone, once both tokens already have a numeraire pool on this hook with the same tick spacing. Otherwise `MultiAsset.initialize` reverts `NumeraireRequired`. The check reads only the hook's storage. |
| Fee | Dynamic-fee flag, as for every pool. |
| Quote side | `currency1`. Orders paying `currency1` are bids, orders paying `currency0` are asks. |
| Minimum order | Each side's decimal floor, `10^(decimals - assetPrecision)` of that token, at least 1 unit. No dollar minimum. |
| Priority bids | Not allowed, since bids are paid in the numeraire. A nonzero `priorityFee` or a top-up reverts `PriorityFeeNeedsNumeraire`. |

The floors stop dust, not small orders: 0.0001 of a cheap token can be worth very little. Stablecoins other than
the numeraire are ordinary tokens here.

# Dutch auction orders

A maker can turn a resting order into a Dutch auction. The order's minimum output starts at its current value and
falls in a straight line to a floor over a number of blocks. Fillers fill it as soon as the price works for them,
so the maker gets a price found by competition rather than a fixed quote. The logic lives in the linked
`DutchAuction` library; the auction record is stored in the hook by order id.

## Start an auction

Place the order as usual, at the price you would like to get. Then call the hook directly:

```solidity
hook.startAuction(order, floorAmountOutMin, duration);
```

* Only the maker can start an auction.
* `floorAmountOutMin` is the least output you accept. It must be above zero, below the order's current minimum,
  and meet the pool's order minimums.
* `duration` is in blocks, from 1 to `DutchAuction.MAX_DURATION` (50,000).
* The hook emits `AuctionStarted(orderId, start, floor, startBlock, duration)`.

The scheduled minimum at block `b` is:

```
start - (start - floor) * (b - startBlock) / duration
```

It rounds in the maker's favour and stays at the floor once the duration ends.

## Steps

`hook.stepAuction(order)` writes the scheduled minimum into the order through the normal reprice path, so the book
always holds a real price. Anyone can call it, untaxed. It does nothing for an order with no running auction, and
returns the order's minimum output after the step.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["stepAuction(order)"] --> A{"Running auction?"}
    A -- "No" --> R["Return the stored minimum"]
    A -- "Yes" --> B{"Order still open and<br/>reprice count unchanged?"}
    B -- "No: closed or maker repriced" --> D["Delete the auction"] --> R
    B -- "Yes" --> C{"Scheduled minimum<br/>below the stored one?"}
    C -- "Yes" --> U["updatePrice to the schedule<br/>AsyncOrderPriceUpdated, fresh time priority"]
    C -- "No" --> E
    U --> E{"Duration over?"}
    E -- "Yes" --> D2["Delete the auction;<br/>order rests at the floor"] --> R
    E -- "No" --> R
```

Between steps the stored minimum is at or above the schedule, so a match or fill never pays the maker less than
the schedule gives. Each step is a reprice: it gives the order fresh time priority and increments its reprice
count, which also voids any reprice the maker signed earlier.

## Fills

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Filler
    participant R as Router
    participant H as AsyncSwap hook
    participant DA as DutchAuction

    alt Flash fill (fillOrderWithCallback, fillOrderInCallback)
        Filler->>R: fill with maxPrice
        R->>H: stepAuction(order)
        H->>DA: step: write the scheduled minimum
        R->>H: asyncOrderInfo: live minimum within maxPrice
        Note over R,H: filler pays the scheduled price, no extra call
    else Plain fill (Router.fillOrder)
        Filler->>H: stepAuction(order), from the filler contract
        Filler->>R: fillOrder(order, maxPrice), same transaction
    else Book match or pool fill
        Filler->>H: stepAuction(order)
        Filler->>R: matchBook or fillFromPoolLiquidity
        Note over Filler,R: send both from one contract to keep them in one transaction
    end
```

Book matches and pool fills use the stored price, so a step is what lets the book see the newer price. `maxPrice`
still binds every filler fill.

## Stop or change an auction

* Cancel the order as usual.
* Or reprice it with `updatePrice` or a signed reprice. A maker reprice stops the auction, and the order then
  rests at the maker's new price.
* Calling `startAuction` again replaces the running schedule, starting from the order's current minimum.

# Signed price changes

```
UpdatePrice(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 newAmountOutMin,bytes32 orderId,uint64 createdSequence,uint32 reprices,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
CancelOrder(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,bytes32 orderId,uint64 createdSequence,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
```

A signed price change identifies one order with `orderId` and `uint64 createdSequence`
(`orderCreatedSequence(poolId, orderId)`), and one price version of it with `uint32 reprices`
(`orderReprices(poolId, orderId)`), the number of times it has been repriced. `amountIn` is the order's
input when signed; the relayer passes it to `updatePriceWithSig(order, amountIn, newAmountOutMin, nonce,
deadline, signature)`.

Every reprice, direct or signed, increments `reprices`, so a reprice signature the maker never relayed
cannot undo a later reprice. Matches do not move it: if partial matches shrink the order before the reprice
lands, the signed `amountIn` and `newAmountOutMin` are applied as a price to the remainder, with the minimum
rounded up, instead of the signature failing (L-01 in
[the 2026-11-01 review](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/lsp_security_review_2026-11-01.md)). A live input larger than the signed
one is rejected. Cancelling and recreating an identical order gives it a new `createdSequence`, so an unused
signature for the cancelled order cannot change the replacement.

Signed cancels bind `createdSequence` but not the order's size: a cancel covers whatever remains.

Earlier versions bound the order's queue `sequence` (which a partial match can also move) and, before that,
`createdSequence` alone; signatures of either kind must be signed again. The original incarnation fix is
described below.

Regression tests reproduce the vulnerability before the fix in Solidity, native Huff, and Python.
After the fix, they check that the old signature is rejected, the replacement minimum and unused nonce
are preserved, and a fresh signature successfully reprices the replacement using that nonce.

Validation: 860 Solidity tests, 238 current Huff tests, and 43 Python model tests passed. Both Foundry
suites skipped one RPC-dependent fork test. Shared stateful/matching/hash vectors passed on both
implementations. Historical Huff storage-specific fixtures remain excluded from its current suite.
The regenerated Lean models build; the added refinement lemmas check the encoder and distinct
creation-sequence preimages, without claiming unconditional hash or signature security.

[Logs and source fingerprints](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/validation/reprice-incarnation-2026-10-24/results.json).

# Priority fee top-ups

Implemented in source; requires a new hook and Router deployment. The existing immutable deployments
and the frozen audit scope do not include this endpoint.

## API

```solidity
router.topUpPriorityFee(order, addedFee);
```

The caller must be `order.owner`, with sufficient USDC balance and ERC-20 allowance to the Router.
A registered filling executor cannot top up another maker's order. Agents can submit from the maker's
wallet or through that wallet's own authorized execution mechanism. There is no new relayed signature
or Permit2 top-up endpoint in this version.

`addedFee` is a positive delta in the numeraire's base units. With six-decimal USDC, `25_000` adds
$0.025. The function identifies the order by chain, pool, owner, direction and salt; the amount,
minimum output and fee supplied in the order struct may be stale. It adds to the bid currently stored
on the order. For example, a $0.10 bid reduced to $0.075 by a partial fill becomes $0.10 after adding
$0.025.

The resulting bid must be at least `min(remaining USDC notional / 1000, pool priorityFeeCap)`, rounded
down. The default cap is $0.10 and limits the required minimum, not the user's maximum bid. A partially
consumed bid may sit below this minimum until amended, but a top-up must bring it back to the current
minimum. The resulting bid cannot exceed `uint64.max` base units. Missing and closed orders revert.

## Priority and settlement

* The limit price and remaining input budget do not change.
* Exact price remains the first ranking rule. A higher bid breaks equal-price ties.
* The order receives a fresh queue sequence and joins behind existing equal-price, equal-fee orders.
* The original maker age and signed reprice version stay unchanged. A pending signed reprice or
  cancellation is not invalidated by a top-up; nonce invalidation remains the way to revoke it.
* Added fees follow the existing non-refundable settlement rule: proportional consumption on fills,
  with the remainder going to the FeeVault on closure or cancellation. They are not keeper rewards.

The Router transfers USDC to PoolManager and credits the hook before the library rekeys the fee
queue and mints the added escrow claims. The price-level bitmap and order counts stay unchanged.
PoolManager requires balanced currency deltas at unlock completion; a payment failure, short payment
or invalid amendment reverts funding and queue changes together. The hook emits:

```solidity
event AsyncOrderPriorityFeeUpdated(
    PoolId indexed poolId, bytes32 indexed orderId, uint256 addedFee, uint256 newPriorityFee
);
```

The update uses the live order after payment. If a token callback partially fills it, the delta is
added to that remainder; if the order closes during payment, the transaction reverts. Supported USDC
transfers do not normally make such callbacks, but this behavior is tested.

## Agent choice: top up, or top up and match

A top-up does not attempt matching and does not pay the Router's native MEV tax. It still costs
transaction gas. Use it when raising priority for future liquidity. When compatible liquidity is
already visible, combine it with a bounded matching call:

```solidity
bytes[] memory calls = new bytes[](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/docs/2);
calls[0] = abi.encodeCall(router.topUpPriorityFee, (order, addedFee));
calls[1] = abi.encodeCall(router.matchBook, (order.key, uint8(8)));
router.multicall(calls);
```

`maxMatches` must be 1–8. The matcher processes the book's best executable pairs, so the targeted
order is not guaranteed a fill within that bound. If no crossing pair exists, matching may succeed
without a fill and the top-up remains committed. If either call reverts, the entire batch reverts.
This is book matching; LP retries remain the separate `fillFromPoolLiquidity` path.

Read the live remaining bid and order state, choose a spending limit, then simulate the exact call
or multicall before submission. Simulation does not reserve liquidity. Retrying the same successful
top-up in a new transaction adds the delta again; check the receipt and current bid before retrying.

For transaction-cost measurements and reproduction instructions, see [the top-up benchmark](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/benchmarks/topups/README.md).

Sources: [Router](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/Router.sol), [hook](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/AsyncSwap.sol),
[fee amendments](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/PriorityFeeUpdates.sol), and
[tests](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/test/PriorityFeeTopUp.t.sol).

# Contract call sequences

The [protocol overview](/protocol/overview#3-placing-an-order) has the short order sequence; this page has the detailed ones. See [order lifecycle and priority bids](/protocol/order-lifecycle) for the flowcharts, [flash fills](/protocol/flash-fills#flow) for the flash-fill sequence and [Dutch auctions](/protocol/dutch-auction#fills) for auction fills.

Solid arrows are calls or actions; dashed arrows are returns or delivered results. Each sequence groups related transactions; it is not one transaction from top to bottom. The app and wallet represent the user interface, not trusted settlement components. An indexer may observe emitted events for discovery, but neither an API nor an indexer is required by the contracts.

`IncomingMatching`, `AsyncMatching`, `MultiAsset` and `DutchAuction` are linked libraries called by DELEGATECALL in the hook's context, and `AsyncFiller` is internal to them, so arrows from them to PoolManager execute as the hook. ERC-6909 claims and LP fee accounting live inside PoolManager. Every Router action is one `PoolManager.unlock` (v4 flash accounting): it can only finish once every delta is zero.

### User order, book matching, and LP fallback

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Maker
    participant App as App
    participant Wallet as Maker wallet
    actor Relayer
    participant Router
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant Match as IncomingMatching / AsyncMatching / AsyncFiller
    participant Fee as DynamicFeeOrdering
    participant Permit as Permit2
    participant Token as ERC-20 / USDC
    participant PM as PoolManager
    actor Counterparty as Resting maker
    participant Vault as FeeVault

    User->>App: Choose asset, input amount, minimum output, and bid
    App->>Wallet: Request approval, authorization, and order confirmation
    opt Router not yet authorized for this maker and pool
        Wallet->>Hook: setExecutor(poolId, Router, true)
        Hook-->>Wallet: Authorization recorded
    end
    Note over Wallet,Token: Direct ERC-20 input needs Router approval, signed input needs Permit2 approval.<br/>A nonzero USDC bid separately needs Router approval.
    alt Direct order, including native ETH input
        Wallet->>Router: swap(order, userData), msg.value = native input + MEV tax
    else Signed ERC-20 order
        Wallet-->>Relayer: Permit2 order-witness signature and optional executor grant
        Relayer->>Router: swapWithSig(order, permit, grant)
        opt Signed executor grant needed
            Router->>Hook: setExecutorWithSig(...)
            Hook-->>Router: Grant validated and recorded
        end
    end
    Router->>PM: unlock(create action)
    PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
    opt Nonzero MEV tax
        Router->>PM: settle the tax in ETH, mint it to FeeVault as native claims
    end
    Router->>PM: swap(exact input, hook data)
    PM->>Hook: beforeSwap(...)
    Hook->>PM: mint input escrow claims to hook
    Hook->>Match: Check minimums and stage crossing arrival, or add to price book
    Match->>PM: mint bid escrow claims to hook, hook owes bid
    Match-->>Hook: Order staged or indexed
    Note over Hook,Match: Without active LPs, potentially crossing arrivals use transient storage during funding.<br/>AsyncOrderCreated is emitted, and matching waits until input and bid funding finish.
    Hook-->>PM: BeforeSwapDelta takes the whole input (custom accounting)
    PM-->>Router: Swap delta
    alt Direct input funding
        Router->>PM: Settle input using ERC-20 transfer or forwarded ETH
    else Permit2 input funding
        Router->>PM: sync(input token)
        Router->>Permit: permitWitnessTransferFrom(order witness)
        Permit->>Token: transferFrom(maker, PoolManager, input)
        Token-->>Permit: Transfer succeeds
        Permit-->>Router: Signature and transfer accepted
        Router->>PM: settle()
    end
    opt Nonzero priority bid
        Router->>PM: sync(USDC)
        Router->>Token: transferFrom(maker, PoolManager, bid)
        Token-->>Router: Transfer succeeds
        Router->>PM: settleFor(hook)
    end
    Router->>Hook: matchNewOrder(order)
    Note over Hook,PM: If the pool has active liquidity and its spot tick beats the best opposing level,<br/>the pool fill below runs first, limited at that level, and the book takes what it leaves.<br/>A remainder below the pool minimum that the book leaves is then refunded as claims.
    Hook->>Match: matchNewOrder(...), recheck liquidity and load candidate
    loop Up to 8 executable crossing pairs
        Match->>Match: Best bid and ask across candidate plus stored book (price, then bid, then time)
        Match->>Match: Reduce both orders before any payout
        Match->>PM: Settle filled bid shares to FeeVault
        Match->>PM: Burn input claims and credit both order legs as claims
        PM-->>Wallet: Proceeds as claims (any currency)
        PM-->>Counterparty: Proceeds as claims (any currency)
        Note over Match,Vault: Re-rank remainders. A remainder below the pool minimum is returned as claims<br/>and its residual bid goes to FeeVault.
    end
    Match->>Match: Persist only the memory candidate's remainder
    Match-->>Hook: Matched pair count
    opt Stored route: incoming order still has a remainder
        Hook->>Hook: External self-call fillOrderFromPoolLiquidity(order, id)
        Hook->>Match: fillFromPoolLiquidity(...)
        Match->>PM: Burn the input claims less 0.01%, temporarily set 0.02% LP fee
        Match->>PM: swap(remaining exact input)
        Note over Hook,PM: Hook-originated swap skips this hook's callbacks, it does not create another order.
        PM-->>Match: Actual input and output deltas
        Match->>PM: Restore previous LP fee
        Match->>PM: Mint back any input the swap left unused (only a swap limited at the book level stops short)
        Match->>PM: transfer 0.01% of the input swapped to FeeVault (protocol fee)
        Match->>Fee: charge(state, key, output, tickBefore, amountOut)
        Note over Fee,PM: First pool fill in a 2-block window: record the tick before it as the reference, no fee.<br/>Later fill in the window that moves the price back toward it: half the price gap it closes.
        opt Dynamic fee is due
            Fee->>PM: donate half of the fee to in-range LPs
            Fee->>PM: mint the rest to FeeVault as claims
        end
        Fee-->>Match: Dynamic fee, taken from the output
        alt Full remaining input consumed and minimum output met after the dynamic fee
            Match->>PM: Pay output less the dynamic fee, settle remaining bid to FeeVault
            PM-->>Wallet: ERC-20 proceeds or native claims
            Match-->>Hook: Order removed, liquidity fill event
        else Pool first, stopped at the book level, pro-rata minimum met
            Match->>Match: Reduce the order, keeping the maker's limit, and settle the filled bid share
            Match->>PM: Credit output less the dynamic fee as claims
            Match-->>Hook: Order stays open for the book, liquidity fill event
        else Insufficient liquidity, partial execution without a limit, or limit not met
            Match-->>Hook: Self-call reverts, caught by matchNewOrder
            Note over Hook,PM: Only LP attempt rolls back, prior book fills and open remainder survive.
        end
    end
    Hook-->>Router: Matched pair count
    Router-->>PM: Callback complete
    PM-->>Router: Unlock completes if all currency deltas are settled
    Router-->>Wallet: Direct transaction succeeds
    Note over Wallet,Relayer: For signed submission, the transaction result returns to the submitter instead.
```

The LP fee and the LPs' half of the dynamic fee accrue through PoolManager's position accounting (the dynamic fee by `donate`); see [`dynamic-fee-ordering.md`](/protocol/dynamic-fee-ordering). Priority bids are not paid to LPs: every settled bid goes to the FeeVault. LPs do not receive an external callback on every fill.

### Private fillers, continuation, repricing, and cancellation

These are alternative actions on open orders. Private fills and LP retries require the Router to remain authorized by the maker. Book continuation is permissionless and processes at most eight pairs per call.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Maker as Maker / wallet
    actor Caller as Filler or public caller
    participant Router
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant Match as AsyncMatching / AsyncFiller
    participant Token as Output ERC-20
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant Vault as FeeVault

    alt Private filler settles a specific order
        Caller->>Hook: asyncOrderInfo(poolId, orderId)
        Hook-->>Caller: Live remaining input and minimum output
        opt Dutch auction order
            Caller->>Hook: stepAuction(order), same transaction
        end
        Caller->>Router: fillOrder(order, maxPrice, data), msg.value = native output + MEV tax
        Note over Caller,Hook: Native output requires exact gross ETH, forwarded by Router to hook before unlock.<br/>ERC-20 output requires filler approval to Router.
        Router->>PM: unlock(fill action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>PM: settle the MEV tax, mint it to FeeVault
        Router->>Hook: Read live input, minimum and surcharge (calculatePoolFee, zero)
        Hook-->>Router: Live input and minimum
        Router->>Router: Require live input at least order.amountIn and the minimum no greater than maxPrice
        opt ERC-20 output
            Router->>PM: sync(output token)
            Router->>Token: transferFrom(filler, PoolManager, gross output)
            Token-->>Router: Transfer succeeds
            Router->>PM: settleFor(hook)
            Router->>Hook: Re-read the order, revert if it changed during the transfer
        end
        Router->>Hook: executeOrder(order, filler)
        Hook->>Match: fill(...), validate executor and open order
        Match->>PM: Settle output, pay maker its minimum less 0.02%
        PM-->>Maker: ERC-20 output or native claims
        Match->>PM: mint the maker's 0.02% as FeeVault claims
        Note over PM,Vault: Claims are credited inside PoolManager, FeeVault is not called during a fill.
        Match->>PM: Burn input escrow, pay filler the input less 0.02%, mint that 0.02% to FeeVault
        PM-->>Caller: ERC-20 input or native claims
        Match->>PM: Settle remaining bid to FeeVault
        Match-->>Hook: Order closed, AsyncOrderFilled event
        Hook-->>Router: Fill complete
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds
    else Continue a crossed book
        Caller->>Router: matchBook(key, maxMatches from 1 to 8)
        Router->>PM: unlock(match action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: matchBook(key, maxMatches)
        Hook->>Match: Match best bid and ask, settle pairs and bids
        Match->>PM: Burn claims, pay counterparties less 0.02% each (to FeeVault), settle bid shares
        Match-->>Hook: Matched pair count
        Hook-->>Router: Matched pair count
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds
    else Retry a specific order against LP liquidity
        Caller->>Router: fillFromPoolLiquidity(order), msg.value = MEV tax
        Router->>PM: unlock(pool fill action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>PM: settle the MEV tax, mint it to FeeVault
        Router->>Hook: tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity(order)
        Note over Hook,PM: Same guarded LP self-call as above, including the dynamic fee, no book-priority check.
        Hook-->>Router: true if filled, false if LP attempt rolled back
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds, inspect events for actual fill
    else Maker reprices
        Maker->>Hook: updatePrice(order, newAmountOutMin)
        Hook->>Match: Update minimum, re-enter with fresh sequence
        Match-->>Hook: New price and rank
        Hook-->>Maker: AsyncOrderPriceUpdated event
        Note over Maker,PM: No Router or PoolManager unlock, this does not trigger matching by itself.
    else Maker cancels
        Maker->>Router: cancelOrder(order)
        Router->>PM: unlock(cancel action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: cancelOrder(order)
        Hook->>Match: Validate owner or executor, remove open order
        Match->>PM: Burn input claims and return remaining input
        PM-->>Maker: ERC-20 refund or native claims
        Match->>PM: Settle non-refundable remaining bid to FeeVault
        Match-->>Hook: AsyncOrderCancelled event
        Hook-->>Router: Cancellation complete
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Maker: Transaction succeeds
    else Maker batches cancels and a withdrawal
        Maker->>Router: multicall([cancelOrder(a), cancelOrder(b), withdrawClaims(currencies, amounts)])
        loop Each call, run by the Router as the maker
            Router->>PM: unlock(that call's action)
            PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
            Router->>Hook: cancelOrder(order), as in the cancel above
            Router->>PM: or burn(maker, claim ID, amount) and take(currency, maker, amount)
            Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        end
        PM-->>Maker: Refunds and withdrawn claims
        Router-->>Maker: Transaction succeeds, or every call reverts together
    end
```

To cancel several orders at once, the maker sends `Router.multicall([cancelOrder(a), cancelOrder(b), ...])`: each call above runs in turn as the maker, with its own unlock, and one failure reverts them all. A `withdrawClaims` call can follow in the same batch. Signed alternatives are `Hook.updatePriceWithSig` and `Router.cancelWithSig`; a relayer can submit the maker's signature. Signature checks precede the corresponding state change or cancellation unlock. Any uncaught revert rolls back the whole transaction, including transfers and bid settlements.

### Pool setup, liquidity providers, and withdrawals

The liquidity manager below is a compatible Uniswap v4 periphery contract, not Async Swap's order Router. Its precise user-facing methods depend on the chosen periphery; the PoolManager calls shown are the common execution path. Setup and withdrawals are separate transactions from order execution.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Operator as Pool initializer
    actor Admin as Protocol owner
    actor LP as Liquidity provider
    actor Holder as Claim holder
    participant LM as v4 liquidity manager
    participant Router
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant Native as NativeClaims
    participant Tokens as TokenClaims
    participant Vault as FeeVault
    actor Recipient

    Operator->>PM: initialize(key, sqrtPriceX96)
    PM->>Hook: beforeInitialize(...)
    Hook->>Hook: MultiAsset.initialize: require the dynamic-fee flag
    alt Pool holds the numeraire
        Hook->>Hook: Copy the deployment minimum order and bid cap to the pool
    else Pool without the numeraire
        Hook->>Hook: Require numeraire pools for both tokens, same tick spacing
        Hook->>Hook: Quote-side floor from currency1 decimals, no priority bids
    end
    Hook->>Hook: Reject an asset with no code, read its decimals and store its 0.0001-token floor
    Hook-->>PM: beforeInitialize selector
    PM-->>Operator: Initialized tick, Initialize event
    LP->>LM: Add funded liquidity in a chosen tick range
    LM->>PM: unlock(liquidity operation)
    PM->>LM: unlockCallback(data)
    LM->>PM: modifyLiquidity(key, params, hookData)
    PM->>Hook: beforeAddLiquidity(...)
    Hook-->>PM: beforeAddLiquidity selector
    PM-->>LM: Liquidity and fee deltas
    LM->>PM: Settle required token amounts
    LM-->>PM: Callback complete
    PM-->>LM: Unlock complete
    LM-->>LP: Position updated
    Note over LP,PM: Eligible positions accrue swap fees in PoolManager accounting.<br/>LPs collect through their chosen liquidity manager, no per-fill LP callback.

    Holder->>PM: approve(NativeClaims, claim ID 0, amount)
    PM-->>Holder: Claim allowance recorded
    Holder->>Native: redeem(recipient, amount)
    Native->>PM: unlock(redemption)
    PM->>Native: unlockCallback(data)
    Native->>PM: burn(holder, native claim ID 0, amount)
    Native->>PM: take(native ETH, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: ETH payment
    Native-->>PM: Callback complete, NativeRedeemed event
    PM-->>Native: Unlock complete
    Native-->>Holder: Redemption complete

    Holder->>PM: approve(TokenClaims, currency claim ID, amount)
    PM-->>Holder: Claim allowance recorded
    Holder->>Tokens: redeem(currency, recipient, amount)
    Tokens->>PM: unlock(redemption)
    PM->>Tokens: unlockCallback(data)
    Tokens->>PM: burn(holder, currency claim ID, amount)
    Tokens->>PM: take(currency, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: ERC-20 payment
    Tokens-->>PM: Callback complete, ClaimsRedeemed event
    PM-->>Tokens: Unlock complete
    Tokens-->>Holder: Redemption complete

    Holder->>PM: approve(Router, each claim ID, exact amount)
    PM-->>Holder: Claim allowances recorded
    Holder->>Router: withdrawClaims(currencies, amounts), up to 16 distinct currencies
    Router->>PM: unlock(withdrawal)
    PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
    Router->>PM: burn(holder, claim ID, amount) and take(currency, holder, amount), per currency
    PM-->>Holder: ERC-20 and ETH payments to the holder's own wallet
    Router-->>PM: Callback complete, ClaimWithdrawn events
    PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
    Router-->>Holder: Withdrawal complete

    Admin->>Vault: collect(currency, recipient)
    Vault->>Hook: owner()
    Hook-->>Vault: Current protocol owner
    Vault->>PM: unlock(fee collection)
    PM->>Vault: unlockCallback(data)
    Vault->>PM: Read and burn FeeVault's currency claims
    Vault->>PM: take(currency, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: Collected fees
    Vault-->>PM: Callback complete, FeesCollected event
    PM-->>Vault: Unlock complete
    Vault-->>Admin: Collection complete
```

Native and ERC-20 redemption require a positive amount, a nonzero recipient and a claim allowance; a failed delivery (ETH rejected, or a token refusing the recipient) reverts the redemption and restores the claims and allowance, and the holder can redeem to another recipient. Fee collection only redeems FeeVault's balances and is restricted to the current hook owner. It cannot redeem maker escrow.

Sources: [Router](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/Router.sol), [AsyncSwap](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/AsyncSwap.sol), [AsyncMatching](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol), [AsyncFiller](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol), [NativeClaims](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/NativeClaims.sol), [TokenClaims](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/TokenClaims.sol), and [FeeVault](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/FeeVault.sol).

# Price keys and crossing

## Price keys

Every resting order is indexed on its pool's book by a `uint128` price key computed in
`AsyncFiller._priceKey` (`TickPrice.key`): the Uniswap v4 tick of the order's exact limit.

1. Take the order's currency1/currency0 ratio: `amountOutMin / amountIn` when it sells currency0,
   `amountIn / amountOutMin` when it sells currency1.
2. Take its floor tick: the largest tick `t` (spacing 1, price `1.0001^t`) priced at or below the
   ratio (`TickPrice.floorTick`, via `TickMath.getTickAtSqrtPrice`).
3. Order ticks by numeraire per asset: `t - MIN_TICK + 1` when the numeraire is currency1,
   `MAX_TICK - t + 1` when it is currency0.

Keys run from `1` to `2 * MAX_TICK + 1`. Ratios outside the v4 price range (about `2^-128` to
`2^128`) share the end keys. Each level is 0.01% wide at any price and for any token decimals,
so two orders sharing a nonclamped key are within approximately 0.01% of each other.
The end levels do not have this spread bound. The exact limit stays on the order:
keys order the radix tree; they do not by themselves decide whether two orders trade.

## Crossing rule

`AsyncMatching._crosses(buyKey, sellKey, buy, sell)` decides whether a buy and a sell can trade:

* `buyKey > sellKey` is a cross and `buyKey < sellKey` is not. The key is monotone in the exact
  price, so a strict ordering of keys always reflects a strict ordering of exact prices.
* Equal keys are decided at full precision:

```
cross  <=>  buyIn / buyOut >= sellOut / sellIn
       <=>  buyIn * sellIn >= sellOut * buyOut
       <=>  floor(buyIn * sellIn / sellOut) >= buyOut      (sellOut and buyOut are nonzero)
```

implemented as `Math.mulDiv(buy.amountIn, sell.amountIn, sell.amountOutMin) >= buy.amountOutMin`.
Orders cannot be created or updated with a zero minimum, so the divisor is never zero. Both escrowed inputs are bounded by signed 128-bit settlement amounts, so their product and
its quotient by a positive minimum fit in 256 bits, including at clamped end levels.

An exact tie (`buyIn * sellIn == sellOut * buyOut`) counts as a cross and executes.

## Consequences

* Equal-key noncrossing heads no longer terminate selection when another pair is eligible.
  Each priority subtree stores its minimum exact ask or maximum exact bid. The search chooses
  the higher-priority child if its summary admits a crossing order, otherwise the other child.
  Each lookup traverses at most 128 branches without scanning or persistent cursors.
* Automatic arrivals and resting-book matching use the same selection rule: the exact highest
  bid and exact lowest ask in their best levels. The subtree extremum is the eligibility threshold,
  so only orders at that exact extremum qualify; remaining fee and sequence break exact-price ties.
  If these extrema do not cross, no pair at the boundary crosses. Prices grouped in the same level
  never let a worse exact price jump ahead by paying more.
* Every genuine cross, including the tie, produces a non-zero match in `_matchAmounts` that pays
  each maker at least their signed minimum for the input consumed. This was checked exhaustively
  for small amounts and on randomized large near-tie pairs.
* Matching compares the signed minimums, not the post-fee proceeds, so the 0.02% trade fee (taken
  from each side's proceeds afterwards, rounded up) never changes which orders cross.

Example of equal keys without a cross: a sell asking `1000.05` and a buy offering `1000.02`
USDC per asset sit on the same tick, but the buy is below the ask, so the pair rests.

## Tests

`test/security/PriceKeyCrossing.t.sol`:

* `test_equalKeyNonCrossingPairDoesNotBlockMatching`
* `test_matchBookMakesNoFalseMatch`
* `test_exactTieExecutes`

## Level width and the price-priority bound

Within one tick, priority is bid then sequence, not exact price, so a higher-bid order can trade
ahead of one priced up to 0.01% better. Across ticks, price always comes first. Under the earlier
WAD-ratio key a level was `10^(assetDecimals - usdcDecimals - 18)` USDC/asset wide, which is
about 10% of the price for an 18-decimal asset at $0.00001, and the clamped keys `1` and
`type(uint128).max` merged arbitrarily distant prices (audit 2026-10-23, finding 1). Ticks remove
both: the width is relative and fixed, and only prices outside the v4 range share the end keys.

## Historical counterexample and repaired regression

`test/security/CoarsePriceBlocking.t.sol` creates a pool with an 18-decimal asset and 6-decimal
USDC fixture at 1,000 USDC/asset, minimum order 1 USDC, and no active LP liquidity. A sell
offering `2e15 - 1` asset base units for `2_000_000` USDC base units has the same key as a
1,000 USDC/asset order, but a slightly higher exact ask. Its `100_001`-unit bid outranks the
`100_000`-unit bids of 20 honest sells. Under the previous head-only policy, twenty matching buys stopped at that blocker, and 100
retries made no progress. The Python `legacy_matching=True` mode preserves that baseline.

With exact eligibility, the same twenty buys execute against the honest sells without cancelling
or outbidding the blocker. The blocker remains open, preserving its escrow and bid. The updated
`CoarsePriceBlockingTest` asserts that outcome through the real Router/hook/PoolManager, and tests
the mirrored incoming-sell case. Generated `EligiblePythonVectors.t.sol` exercises normal prices,
both clamps, blockers on both sides, mutations, partial fills, balances and fee claims.

With tick keys the blocker above is one level worse than the honest asks, so it cannot outrank
them at all. A level is 0.01% of the price wide. That bounds price separation, not delay or backlog.
The repaired selector guarantees finding a crossing pair in a valid book when one exists;
successful settlement and transaction submission remain required. It does not guarantee that
every low-priority order eventually fills under continuing higher-priority arrivals.

The companion model is in the local uv4 checkout under `src/uv4/priority_protocol/`, with results
and explicit modeling boundaries in `docs/priority_protocol/`. `PriorityPythonVectors.t.sol` checks
100 independently generated Python matching cases against the real matcher;
`PriorityPythonHashes.t.sol` checks order identities and signature struct hashes.

## Maintenance, gas, and verification boundaries

`EligiblePrice.sol` compares full 512-bit cross products and stores two-word exact bounds at
priority-tree nodes. Append/remove repair the affected ancestor path. Every partial fill refreshes
the bound even if neither the tick key nor the remaining fee changes. New storage is appended
to each price level; existing live trees would need their summaries initialized before using this
code. These local changes have not been deployed.

The protocol-controlled index work is O(128 M) for M matches. Eight is the existing per-call cap,
not a per-transaction cap. Token code and external settlement costs are outside this structural
bound. `EligibleGas.t.sol` measures composed batches through a real unlock; no numerical
worst-case gas certificate or universally optimal batch size is claimed.

The updated whitepaper is in the local `asyncswap/whitepaper` checkout. Its new section contains
integer safety and search arguments, gas curves, and the constrained parameter objective.

# Dynamic fee ordering

A large order that fills against pool liquidity moves the pool price. Whoever trades the price back
earns the difference: a **backrun**. With only a static fee, that profit goes entirely to the
backrunner, and the LPs whose liquidity absorbed both trades lose it. Since v1.1.0, **dynamic fee
ordering** charges a pool fill that moves the price back a **dynamic fee** sized to the gap it closes,
and splits it between the LPs and the protocol.

The dynamic fee applies only to pool fills (`fillFromPoolLiquidity`, including the pool attempt when a
new order arrives). Book matches and filler fills settle at the orders' signed limits, move no pool
price and don't pay it.

## How it works

The logic is in [`DynamicFeeOrdering.sol`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/DynamicFeeOrdering.sol), a linked library
that `AsyncMatching` calls after every pool fill.

1. **Reference.** Each pool stores a reference tick and the block it was set in
   (`AsyncFiller.State.refTick`, `refBlock`). The first pool fill after the window has expired records
   the pool's tick from *before* that fill as the new reference, and pays no dynamic fee.
2. **Window.** The reference holds for `ORDERING_WINDOW` = 2 blocks after the block that set it. A
   pool fill after that starts a new window.
3. **Dynamic fee.** A pool fill inside the window that ends closer to the reference than it started
   pays

   ```text
   fee = min(amountOut × (gapBefore + gapAfter) / 40_000, amountOut / 2)
   ```

   where `gapBefore` and `gapAfter` are the distances, in ticks, from the reference to the pool's tick
   before and after the fill. If the fill crosses the reference, `gapAfter` is 0 and `amountOut` is only
   the share of the output from the side before the reference, `amountOut × gapBefore / (gapBefore +
   ticks past the reference)`: the part past the reference closes no gap and pays nothing. One tick is about 0.01%, so `(gapBefore + gapAfter) / 2` is the average
   price gap over the fill in basis points, and the fee is **half the price gap the fill closes**.
4. **No dynamic fee** for a fill that moves the price further from the reference, or doesn't move it.
5. **Split.** Half the dynamic fee is donated to in-range LPs (`PoolManager.donate`). The other half,
   plus any rounding, is credited to the FeeVault as ERC-6909 claims. If no liquidity is in range
   after the fill, all of it goes to the FeeVault.
6. **Maker protection.** The dynamic fee is taken from the fill's output before the maker is paid, and
   the output that remains must still meet the order's minimum. Otherwise the pool fill reverts, and
   the order goes to the book or rests, exactly as when a pool fill misses its limit for any other
   reason.

The 0.01% protocol fee on the input and the 0.02% LP fee still apply to every pool fill; the dynamic
fee is on top of them.

Each charge emits `DynamicFeeCharged(poolId, orderId, currency, toLps, toFeeVault, refTick)` from the
hook: the fill's output currency, the LPs' and the FeeVault's shares, and the reference tick it was
measured against. The fill's `AsyncOrderLiquidityFilled` reports the maker's output after the fee.

Every successful pool fill also emits `PoolPriceObserved(poolId, orderId, tickBefore, tickAfter, refTick, observedBlock)`. Indexers can use these events as a price-movement log to identify large tick moves and evaluate fee settings. The contract stores only the current reference tick and block; it does not need a full on-chain price history to calculate the fee, which continues to scale with the tick gap the fill closes.

## Example

From [`test/BackrunCapture.t.sol`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/test/BackrunCapture.t.sol), a pool at 1 USDC per asset with deep
liquidity:

| | Before v1.1.0 | v1.1.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Alice sells 2,000 asset into the pool | price drops | price drops; reference set |
| Bob buys back with the USDC Alice received, same block | static fees only | pays the dynamic fee |
| Bob's profit, valued at the pre-sell price | 3.39 USDC | 1.34 USDC |
| LPs and FeeVault capture from Bob's backrun | about 0.6 USDC | 2.65 USDC |

Bob still profits, so pools keep getting brought back to the market price, but most of the gap now
stays with the LPs and the protocol.

## Splitting a backrun

A fee charged per swap invites splitting: several small backruns each pay a lower rate. Here the
dynamic fee depends on the gap at each fill's start and end, not on how many fills there are.
Splitting one backrun into several orders pays roughly the same total, because each piece pays on the
part of the gap it closes. In the test, five orders earn 1.38 USDC against 1.34 for one; the small
difference comes from averaging the gap linearly in ticks while the pool's price curve is not linear.

## What it doesn't cover

* **The dynamic fee is in the output currency.** A backrun that buys the asset pays it in the asset;
  one that sells the asset pays in USDC. Valued at the reference price, the two are the same.
* **Only within the window.** A backrun that lands more than 2 blocks after the fill that set the
  reference pays nothing. On chains with short block times, such as Unichain, that's a few seconds.
* **One reference per window.** If several large fills happen in one window, they're all measured
  against the price before the first one.
* **It's an estimate.** The gap is measured in ticks against the pool's own earlier price, not against
  an outside market price. A fill that moves the pool back after the outside market really moved
  still pays within the window.
* **Not in formal proofs.** The Foundry tests and the uv4 Python model cover it.

## Deployment

`DynamicFeeOrdering` is linked into `AsyncMatching`, which is linked into the hook. `script/deploy.sh`
deploys it through the shared CREATE2 deployer (`script/00_DeployDynamicFeeOrdering.s.sol`, salt
`asyncswap.v2.DynamicFeeOrdering`) before `AsyncMatching`, and records it in `deployments/<chainId>/`.

The current testnet addresses and hook start blocks below match the per-chain deployment registries.

| Hook start block | 67,049,925 | 149,102,588 | 26,826,205 |

How to read the table:

* **`AsyncSwap`, `Router`, `FeeVault`** are the protocol. The hook address is mined per chain for
  its Uniswap v4 permission bits, so it differs by chain, and `FeeVault` is created by the hook's
  constructor. Router addresses depend on the deployer nonce on each chain.
* **`AsyncMatching`, `TickPrice`, `DynamicFeeOrdering`, `TickBitmap`, `EligiblePrice`, `PriorityFeeUpdates`** (and, on Elysium, `IncomingMatching`) are linked libraries, created through the
  deterministic CREATE2 deployer (`0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C`) with fixed salts.
  Identical bytecode gets the same address on every chain. Elysium's later build changed four of them, so
  those addresses differ there.
* **Pool parameters are fixed at deployment.** No setter changes them and anyone can open a pool. On
  these hooks `minOrder` is 0 (no dollar minimum) and `assetPrecision` is 4: an order's asset side
  must be at least 0.0001 of a whole token, or 10^(decimals - 4) base units. The optional priority bid's
  minimum is capped at $0.10, derived from the numeraire's decimals. Routers batch calls with `multicall`.
* **`WithdrawalRouter` entries in the registries are not for these hooks.** They were deployed for
  earlier hooks and are kept as a record. Cancels and claims go through the `Router` above.
* **PoolManager** is the Uniswap v4 singleton the hook is attached to. Unichain Sepolia and
  Robinhood testnet use existing instances. Elysium testnet has no canonical Uniswap v4 instance, so
  its PoolManager was deployed with the protocol.
* **Numeraire** is the stablecoin every pool is priced in.
* **Hook start block** is where an indexer should start reading the hook's events.

The per-chain registries in [`deployments/`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/deployments) are the source of truth: each
`deployments/<chainId>/<chainId>.json` holds every address with its deployment transaction and start
block. The docs site serves all of them, with each chain's name, explorer and numeraire, as one file
at [`/deployments.json`](https://docs.asyncswap.org/deployments.json).

## v1.3.0 release and previous orders

The protocol source is frozen at `c9372ff9577ba3950fa321090a7bfb559fc964a4`.
The deployer and hook owner on both testnets is `0x33ce69DA05c3ad30A3b525625F950fAda8673205` (`new-deployer`).
The registries advertise `features.priorityFeeTopUps: true` only for these new hooks and Routers.

Orders and pools are tied to their hook address. Existing orders remain on the previous deployment and must
be cancelled, filled or claimed through its original Router. They are not migrated to the new book.
The complete previous records are preserved in
[Unichain Sepolia](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/deployments/1301/1301-pre-v1.3.0.json) and
[Robinhood testnet](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/deployments/46630/46630-pre-v1.3.0.json).
Clients and indexers must retain those addresses while adding the new deployment; publishing this registry
alone does not update a running frontend or indexer.

The live create → top-up → cancel sequence passed on both networks. All nine release modules per chain
have exact source matches on Sourcify. See [release validation](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/benchmarks/releases/README.md) for
receipts, measured gas and verification links.
