## Deploying

`script/deploy.sh <chain-key> [dry-run|broadcast|verify]` deploys the libraries (when missing), the
hook and the Router, then writes the registry. Each network has a wrapper:
`deploy-unichain-sepolia.sh` and `deploy-robinhood-testnet.sh`. Chain addresses come from
[`script/config/chains.json`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/script/config/chains.json); RPCs and the keystore account come from
`.env.deploy` (see [`.env.deploy.example`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/.env.deploy.example)).

Fund the deployer with the network's gas token first.

Set `DEPLOYER_ACCOUNT=new-deployer` and its public address as `DEPLOY_OWNER` in the local `.env.deploy`. With that keystore enrolled in Olive, one Touch ID authorization lets Foundry sign the commands in the wrapper:

```bash
olive exec new-deployer -- script/deploy-robinhood-testnet.sh broadcast
```

`verify` submits every registry
entry to Sourcify, then to the chain's Blockscout explorer when there is one, and writes standard
JSON inputs to `deployments/<chainId>/verify/` for manual upload.

# Audit scope: Async Swap (2026-11-05)

Supersedes the [2026-11-03 scope](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/c9372ff/audit/AUDIT_SCOPE_11_03_26.md),
which froze protocol code at `2739d6c`. The prior findings and their dispositions are carried forward below;
passing tests are validation evidence, not a new security audit.

* **Repository:** [asyncswap/contracts](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts)
* **Protocol and production deployment code frozen at:** `c9372ff9577ba3950fa321090a7bfb559fc964a4` on `main`.
  This includes the bitmap optimization (#77) and funded fee top-ups (#78). Check out this exact commit for
  the protocol review. Later release evidence and integration work do not change this frozen source.
* **Compiler:** solc 0.8.26, optimizer on (`optimizer_runs = 10_000`); see `foundry.toml`.
* **Chain:** Unichain (130) first; any EVM chain with Uniswap v4 later.
* **Builds on:** Uniswap v4 `PoolManager` (hooks, ERC-6909 claims, dynamic LP fee), Permit2 for signed orders,
  OpenZeppelin `SafeERC20`, `EIP712`, `SignatureChecker` and `Multicall`.

## Changes since the last freeze (`2739d6c`)

* **Bounded outer tick bitmap.** `TickBitmap` replaces the outer radix price index in `AsyncFiller.Book`;
  the inner Patricia priority tree remains. Check tick boundaries, empty levels, best-price selection and
  count consistency. This changes storage layout and requires a new deployment; no in-place migration exists.
* **Linked exact-price updates.** `EligiblePrice.refresh/remove` are now public linked-library calls to
  keep matching bytecode deployable. Verify caller storage layout, link addresses and summary repair.
* **Funded fee top-ups.** `Router.topUpPriorityFee(order, addedFee)` authenticates the maker, transfers the
  delta in the numeraire and credits the hook before `PriorityFeeUpdates` rekeys the inner queue and mints
  claims. The resulting remaining bid must meet the current minimum and fit uint64. Only the trusted Router
  can enter the hook endpoint. Price, input budget, original maker age and signed-reprice version stay intact;
  fee-tier FIFO age resets. Top-ups are non-refundable, untaxed by the Router's native MEV tax and do not
  invoke matching. Makers can batch a bounded matching call with multicall.
* **Payment callbacks and signatures.** The amendment reads live state after payment. A partial fill during
  payment changes the remainder to which the delta is added; closure reverts the entire transaction.
  Existing signed reprices and cancellations remain valid unless their own validity conditions change.
* **Deployment links.** Production and local deployment wrappers now link `TickBitmap`, `EligiblePrice`,
  and `PriorityFeeUpdates`, in dependency order. A supplied matcher override must match this build's
  predicted address; having code alone is insufficient.
* **Validation.** Independent linear-scan matching-model tests, bitmap boundary/property tests, funding
  and callback regressions, mixed top-up invariants, and public-Router gas measurements accompany the changes.

## What it is

Async Swap is a Uniswap v4 hook that turns swaps into limit orders. Makers escrow their input in the hook and set a
minimum output. Every pool pairs an asset with USDC (the numeraire). Orders are filled by matching against each
other, by permissionless fillers, or against the pool's own liquidity.

* **Pools.** Anyone can create a pool: the hook accepts one that pairs the configured USDC with an asset that has
  code and uses the dynamic-fee flag. The owner cannot open, close or configure pools.
* **Book.** Orders sit at price levels on v4 ticks (`TickPrice`: the floor tick of the exact limit, 0.01% apart).
  The outer index is a bounded bitmap. Within a level they rank by exact limit, then escrowed priority bid, then arrival (`EligiblePrice`); exact
  rational limits decide crossing. New orders and any crossed backlog share one book-wide selection, at most eight
  pairs per call.
* **Venue choice.** A new order goes to the better venue first (`TickPrice.poolBeatsLevel`). If the pool's price
  beats the best opposite level (inside the dynamic-fee window, counting the fee a fill back toward the reference
  would pay), the pool goes first, limited one tick short of that level and inside v4's price range, and the book
  matches the rest. Otherwise the book goes first and the pool must take all of any remainder. A pool fill that
  would leave no active liquidity reverts.
* **Fees.** Book matches and filler fills take 0.02% from what each side receives. Pool fills pay active LPs 0.02%
  and the protocol 0.01%, plus a dynamic fee (`DynamicFeeOrdering`) on a fill that moves the price back toward the
  first pool fill's starting tick within 2 blocks: half the gap it closes, half to LPs and half to `FeeVault`.
* **Settlement.** Book matches credit both sides, and any remainder left below the pool minimum, as PoolManager
  ERC-6909 claims, batched per call (`ClaimTransfers`). Holders redeem them through `TokenClaims` (ERC-20),
  `NativeClaims` (ETH) or `Router.withdrawClaims`. Filler fills and full pool fills pay ERC-20 output directly; native
  output, and a pool fill that leaves part of the order on the book, are credited as claims.
* **Priority bids.** Optional, paid in USDC and escrowed when the order is created. Each fill settles its
  proportional share and the rest settles when the order closes. Every settled bid goes to `FeeVault`, never to LPs. Makers may add funded USDC to the remaining bid through the Router; this changes fee priority without changing their limit price.
* **Minimums.** Fixed at deployment, no setter: an optional minimum order in USDC (`minOrder`, from a dollar amount
  and the numeraire's decimals; 0 by default) and an asset floor per pool (`minAssetAmount`, 10^(decimals − 4), so
  0.0001 of a token). The $0.10 bid cap is derived from the numeraire's decimals too.
* **Signed actions.** Permit2 order witnesses (`swapWithSig`), `SetExecutor`, `UpdatePrice` (binds the order's
  `createdSequence` and its `reprices` count; a reprice that lands after partial matches applies its signed price
  to the remainder) and `CancelOrder` (no order size: covers whatever remains). All use unordered nonces in one space.
* **Router.** The single trusted entry for order creation, and an executor makers can't revoke. `multicall` batches
  actions as the caller (not payable). Order creation and fills pay an MEV tax of the transaction's priority fee
  times `MEV_TAX_GAS` (per chain, fixed at deployment: 20,000,000 on Unichain and Unichain Sepolia, which order by
  priority fee), in `msg.value` on top of any native deposit, credited to `FeeVault` as native claims. The Router can
  cancel for a maker without an executor grant.

Non-blank lines outside comments, using the same count that reproduces the prior 2,704 nSLOC.
There are 21 Solidity source files. Changes are relative to `2739d6c`; a zero line-count delta can still
contain a security-relevant change.

The linked libraries are `AsyncMatching`, `TickPrice`, `DynamicFeeOrdering`, `TickBitmap`, `EligiblePrice`
and `PriorityFeeUpdates`. Calls execute against hook storage. CREATE2 addresses depend on bytecode and
all linked dependencies, not merely the library name or salt.

### Supporting deployment review

Review these frozen files for the release, alongside the protocol security review: `script/deploy.sh`,
`script/local/up.sh`, `script/01_DeployHook.s.sol`, the six `00_Deploy*` library scripts,
`script/DeployTokenClaims.s.sol`, `script/DeployNativeClaims.s.sol`, `script/check-contract-sizes.py`,
`script/config/chains.json`, `script/config/UniswapAddresses.sol` and `script/FFIHelper.sol`.
Check dependency order and exact linked addresses, hook permission flags, constructor values, Router/hook
pairing, claim-redeemer PoolManager identity, registry start blocks and bytecode verification. These
supporting files are not included in the protocol nSLOC total. Operational rehearsals remain separate
from proof that the protocol is secure.

## Trust assumptions

* **Owner** (two-step `transferOwnership` / `acceptOwnership`): sweeps tokens sent to the hook by mistake (`sweep`;
  escrow lives in PoolManager claims, not the hook's balance) and collects fees, bids and MEV tax from `FeeVault`.
  It cannot open, close or configure pools or change minimums. Must not be able to take makers' escrow.
* **Router**: the hook trusts its immutable `router` as the only order-creation path, as an executor no maker can
  revoke, for grant-free cancels on a maker's behalf (the Router checks the owner or a signature), and for burning
  cancel nonces, and for maker-authorized, funded priority-fee amendments. A generic executor grant does not authorize spending a maker's USDC for top-ups.
* **Executors**: a maker authorizes executors per pool (`setExecutor` or `setExecutorWithSig`) and can revoke any of
  them except the Router. An executor can only act on that maker's orders.
* **Fillers / matchers / keepers**: anyone; permissionless.
* **Pool creators**: anyone, for any asset with code. A malicious asset must only be able to affect its own pool.
* **Tokens**: USDC plus standard ERC-20s and native ETH. Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens are not supported.

## Known issues (do not report)

Acknowledged in the reviews below:

* **Ways to race without the MEV tax** (Pashov 4, 5, 6, 9): a searcher can reprice its own resting order with
  `updatePrice` and settle it with `matchBook` (on the Router or directly on the hook, which needs no unlock), or
  pool-fill its own order through `tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity` with its own contract as executor. No user loses
  funds; the tax covers Router creation and fills only.
* **A partly matched order can fall behind an equal-priced order** (Pashov 7): the remainder's minimum rounds up, so
  its exact limit is one unit worse than the maker signed and its bid buys no priority. Pinned by
  `test_knownIssue_partlyMatchedOrderFallsBehindAnEqualOrder`.
* **Fees round to zero on dust orders** (LSP I-01): only with minimums off.
* **The MEV tax needs an exact `msg.value`**: the deposit plus `priority fee × MEV_TAX_GAS`. Wallets should send taxed
  calls with no priority fee; the app does.

By design:

* **A top-up is an additive action.** Repeating it in a new transaction spends the delta again. It resets fee-tier
  age, not maker age, and does not invalidate a previously signed cancellation or reprice. A multicall can
  commit a top-up even when matching succeeds with zero fills. These are explicit semantics, not fill guarantees.

* **Makers can't revoke the Router.** A maker who wants out cancels its orders (through the Router, by signature,
  or directly from its own unlock); the Router acts for a maker only when that maker calls it or signs.

* **Priority bids and top-ups are non-refundable.** All of a bid goes to `FeeVault`, including on cancellation or a dust close.

* **Tokens with recipient callbacks (e.g. ERC-777)** are not supported. Matching pays only claims and runs no
  recipient code; filler fills and full pool fills transfer ERC-20 output after the order is closed.

* **Proceeds are claims.** Recipients redeem through `TokenClaims`, `NativeClaims` or `Router.withdrawClaims`.

* **`DeployWithdrawalRouter`** deploys a testnet-only second Router for claims; the hook trusts only its own Router,
  so cancels through the second one fail.

* `MatchingEngine.sol` is a benchmark harness, not deployed (AuditAgent finding 8, acknowledged).

* Release items in `MAINNET_READINESS.md` (deployment rehearsal, bytecode pinning, throughput stress, deploying the
  claim redeemers) are operational, not code findings.

The 29 leads in the Pashov review and the leads in the LSP review are unconfirmed trails, not known issues:
confirming or ruling out any of them is in scope.

## Previous reviews

Reports are linked at `2739d6c`, the last commit that tracks them. Every fix has a regression test, in
`test/security/` (including `test/security/poc/` and `test/security/PashovFindings.t.sol`),
`test/nethermind_auditagent/` or `test/formal/RoutingPoolImpact.t.sol`.

| Report | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Lee, 33 Labs (2026-05-08) | Earlier design, never launched (`asyncswap/protocol`) | C-01, H-01..H-04, L-02, L-03, I-01 fixed; L-01 works as intended |
| H-05 follow-up (2026-08-08) | Earlier design | H-05 fixed; native reentrancy hardening |
| AI-assisted review (2026-10-10) | Earlier design at `760699a` | M-01, M-02, L-01..L-03, I-01, I-03 fixed; I-02 acknowledged |
| Pre-freeze review (2026-10-19) | Matching engine | Unpaid priority bid could freeze a pool: fixed in #9 |
| [Nethermind AuditAgent 1](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/auditagent_report_1_ae602e60-d592-45ec-92ef-891968f087f0.md) (scan `ae602e60`) | `e04668e` | 12 findings and 2 related issues: all fixed except 8, acknowledged for the harness and fixed live; [status](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/auditagent_report_1_status.md) |
| [Nethermind AuditAgent 2](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/auditagent_report_2_e73aa801-4ee2-4796-9bf6-5ee08d526d36.md) (scan `e73aa801`) | Exact pricing, repricing, cancels | 3 findings fixed; [status](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/auditagent_report_2_status.md) |
| [Formal Mind swarm](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/formal-mind.md) | Routing | FM-01 (Medium): best-price routing bypassed better book liquidity; fixed in `550b463` ([report](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/FM-01-routing-pool-impact.md)) |
| [LSP security review](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/lsp_security_review_2026-11-01.md) (2026-11-01) | `81ba6b8` | M-01, M-02, L-01, L-02 fixed; I-01 acknowledged |
| [Pashov `solidity-auditor`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/2739d6c/audit/pashov_security_review_2026-11-01.md) (2026-11-01, 3 passes) | `7d09cfa` | 1, 2, 3, 8, 10, 11 fixed; 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 acknowledged |

The findings of the last three reviews, in full:

| Review | ID | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Formal Mind | FM-01 | Medium | Best-price routing compares only the pool spot tick, then swaps the whole order through the pool | Fixed |
| LSP | M-01 | Medium | A leftover signed `SetExecutor` grant from `swapWithSig` can undo a maker's revocation | Fixed |
| LSP | M-02 | Medium | A front-run ask can force a new order onto the book at a worse price than the pool | Fixed |
| LSP | L-01 | Low | A small partial match voids a maker's relayed cancel or reprice | Fixed |
| LSP | L-02 | Low | Pool squatting before a token is deployed disables its asset floor | Fixed |
| LSP | I-01 | Info | Fee rounding on dust remainders (only with minimums off) | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 1 | 90 | The backrun fee charges the whole output of a fill that crosses the reference tick | Fixed |
| Pashov | 2 | 90 | A dust order at the end key turns off pool fills for the other side | Fixed |
| Pashov | 3 | 85 | The venue choice ignores the dynamic fee | Fixed |
| Pashov | 4 | 85 | A maker that sets itself as executor fills from the pool with no MEV tax | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 5 | 85 | A direct `updatePrice` makes an old order cross with no MEV tax | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 6 | 85 | Reprice plus `matchBook` pays no MEV tax | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 7 | 75 | Ceil rounding on a partial match makes the remainder's limit worse | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 8 | 75 | A pool-first fill parks the price in an empty range and freezes pool fills | Fixed |
| Pashov | 9 | 75 | Any caller runs the hook's `matchBook` with no unlock and no Router | Acknowledged |
| Pashov | 10 | 75 | A copied executor grant submitted first reverts the relayer's `swapWithSig` | Fixed |
| Pashov | 11 | 75 | The pool-first limit stops one tick past the best resting price | Fixed |

Pashov's column is the reviewer's confidence, not a severity.

## Testing

At the freeze commit (PR #78 validation):

* `forge test`: **1,024 passing, 0 failing, 0 skipped, 184 suites**, including the three pinned Unichain fork
  tests at block 61,709,000. Default solc 0.8.26; optimizer 10,000 runs. PR CI also passed with pinned Foundry 1.8.6.
* Invariants retain 64 runs × depth 64 with fail-on-revert. Handlers now interleave fee top-ups with submission,
  cancellation, repricing, matching, claim redemption and LP fills. They check escrow obligations, conservation
  and best exact-price/fee/age selection.
* `MatchingReference.t.sol` independently scans orders and calculates settlement. Fuzz campaigns use 256 runs
  of 64 mixed operations, plus deterministic backlog, maker-age and dust-closure cases. The model shares
  `TickPrice` only for the documented age reset when rounding moves an order to another tick.
* `PriorityFeeTopUp.t.sol` covers ownership, funding failure/short payment, zero/max bids, minimum admission,
  partial fills, both numeraire positions, configured decimals, multicall rollback and payment callbacks.
  `SignedOrders.t.sol` checks pending signed reprices and cancellations after top-ups.
* The **old freeze's coverage percentages have not been rerun for this source** and are not current coverage
  claims. The formal fixtures are executable bytecode checks; legacy Lean models are not maintained proofs
  of this release.
* Runtime sizes (limit 24,576 bytes): hook 24,159; matcher 24,225; Router 23,061; fee-amendment library 5,537;
  bitmap 696; exact-price library 1,966. Hook/matcher headroom is 417/351 bytes.
* [Bitmap measurements](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/benchmarks/orderbook/README.md) compare the prior radix book with the optimized
  book before top-ups. [Top-up measurements](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/benchmarks/topups/README.md) use actual Router receipts:
  186,710–235,267 gas over four fixtures, including intrinsic gas and refunds, excluding approvals/setup.
  Neither is a production-throughput guarantee.

```sh
git checkout c9372ff9577ba3950fa321090a7bfb559fc964a4
forge build
python3 script/check-contract-sizes.py
forge test
```

## Deployments

The v1.3.0 testnet registries record new hooks, Routers and linked libraries for this frozen source.
Previous deployment records remain available for existing orders. No in-place storage migration exists.
Unichain Sepolia uses test USDC; Robinhood testnet uses test USDG. See [deployments](/deployments)
for addresses, receipt blocks and release evidence. Testnet deployment does not clear the mainnet audit gate.
See [mainnet readiness](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/MAINNET_READINESS.md) for the remaining audit and operational gates.

# Contract reference

These pages are generated by `forge doc` from the NatSpec comments in
[`src/`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/tree/main/src) on every docs build, so they always
match the code on `main`. Each page links to its source file.

| Contract | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [AsyncSwap](/reference/src/AsyncSwap) | The Uniswap v4 hook: turns swaps into orders, escrows input and bids, entry point for matching, fills and cancels. |
| [Router](/reference/src/Router) | Entry point for makers, fillers and relayers: `swap`, `fillOrder`, `cancelOrder`, `cancelAndWithdraw`, `withdrawClaims`, signed variants, `matchBook`, `fillFromPoolLiquidity`, and `multicall` to batch them. |
| [AsyncMatching](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncMatching) | Linked library that matches the book, fills from pool liquidity and settles each pair. |
| [AsyncFiller](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncFiller) | Order storage and the per-pool book: placement, fills, cancels, repricing, bid settlement. |
| [FeeVault](/reference/src/FeeVault) | Holds protocol fee and bid claims; the owner collects them. |
| [TokenClaims](/reference/src/TokenClaims) | Redeems ERC-20 PoolManager claims, such as match proceeds, to any recipient. |
| [NativeClaims](/reference/src/NativeClaims) | Redeems native ETH claims to any recipient. |
| [RadixPriceTree](/reference/src/libraries/RadixPriceTree) and [EligiblePrice](/reference/src/libraries/EligiblePrice) | The price index and the exact-price summaries that find the best crossing order. |

`MatchingEngine` is a standalone benchmark harness and is not deployed.

# AsyncSwap

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/AsyncSwap.sol)

**Inherits:** [BaseHook](/reference/src/BaseHook), EIP712

**Title:** AsyncSwap

**Author:** @msakiart

Uniswap v4 hook that converts an exact-input swap into an open async order: the maker
deposits their input via `_beforeSwap`. Crossing orders settle directly at the resting
limit; fillers settle unmatched orders.

Makers can also act by EIP-712 signature (`setExecutorWithSig`, `updatePriceWithSig`) so a
relayer pays gas and the wallet shows a readable message. See `OrderSignatures` for types.

## Constants

### feeVault

Holds fee claims separately from open-order escrow.

```solidity
FeeVault public immutable feeVault;
```

### numeraire

Chain-specific USDC address. Every pool must include this exact currency.

```solidity
Currency public immutable numeraire;
```

### router

The only swap caller the hook accepts, fixed at deployment. Only the Router settles a new order's input
and hands it to `matchNewOrder`, so an order opened through any other caller would leave the
transient pending-match id set for the rest of the transaction, and `matchBook` would skip that pool.

```solidity
address public immutable router;
```

### minOrder

Minimum order in numeraire base units (0: none), fixed at deployment for every pool so the
owner cannot change the rules under live orders.

```solidity
uint256 public immutable minOrder;
```

### priorityFeeCap

$0.10 in numeraire base units, `10^(decimals - 1)`: the most a priority-bid floor can require.

```solidity
uint64 public immutable priorityFeeCap;
```

### assetPrecision

Decimal places of a whole asset token an order may trade, fixed at deployment: with 4, every order
trades at least 0.0001 token on its asset side. 36 or more leaves only a 1-unit floor.

```solidity
uint8 public immutable assetPrecision;
```

### PENDING_NATIVE_DEPOSIT_SLOT

<i>
  Transient slot — keccak256("asyncswap.hook.pendingNativeDeposit") - 1.
  Tracks ETH deposited to this contract within the current tx via
  `receive()`, so `executeOrder` can settle native output only out of
  the filler's just-received deposit rather than the contract's
  accumulated balance (which may include donations, stranded ETH,
  or in-flight native-input escrow). Cleared after each settle.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_NATIVE_DEPOSIT_SLOT = 0x9c2a7e4f3b1d8a5c6e0f2d4b7a9c1e3d5f8b6a0c2e4d7b9f1a3c5e7d9b1f3a50;
```

### PENDING_MATCH_ID_SLOT

<i>
  Transient hand-off from `_beforeSwap` to the Router after it settles the new input.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_MATCH_ID_SLOT = 0x247d5e35be7fbfd4d95fd66ea940bfb4ee942bef70db6afae46dc83ce0f89eb2;
```

### PENDING_MATCH_EXECUTOR_SLOT

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_MATCH_EXECUTOR_SLOT = 0x9583e36f799bab8c4d06dc676d85ba05b4dfbde5934d5684d8e431d0fd3948da;
```

## State Variables

### asyncOrders

Per-pool order book.

```solidity
mapping(PoolId poolId => AsyncFiller.State) public asyncOrders;
```

### priceBooks

```solidity
mapping(PoolId poolId => AsyncFiller.Book) private priceBooks;
```

### owner

Protocol owner authorized to collect vault fees and sweep stranded balances.

```solidity
address public owner;
```

### pendingOwner

Address nominated by `transferOwnership`; becomes owner on `acceptOwnership`.

```solidity
address public pendingOwner;
```

### nonceUsed

Unordered nonces consumed by signed maker actions (`setExecutorWithSig`, `updatePriceWithSig`).

```solidity
mapping(address maker => mapping(uint256 nonce => bool)) public nonceUsed;
```

### auctions

<i>
  Running Dutch auctions by order id; see `DutchAuction`. Last, so earlier slots keep their places.
</i>

```solidity
mapping(bytes32 orderId => DutchAuction.Auction) private auctions;
```

## Functions

<a id="onlyowner" />

### onlyOwner

Restricts a call to the protocol owner.

```solidity
modifier onlyOwner();
```

<a id="constructor-ipoolmanager-currency-address-address-uint256-uint8" />

### constructor

```solidity
constructor(
        IPoolManager _poolManager,
        Currency _numeraire,
        address _owner,
        address _router,
        uint256 _minOrderUsd,
        uint8 _assetPrecision
    ) BaseHook(_poolManager) EIP712("AsyncSwap", "1");
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \_poolManager | `IPoolManager` |  |
| \_numeraire | `Currency` |  |
| \_owner | `address` | Explicit protocol owner. Not `msg.sender`: CREATE2 deployments run the<br />constructor from the deterministic deployer, which could never act as owner. |
| \_router | `address` | The Router, deployed after the hook (it takes the hook in its constructor): pass its<br />predicted address. |
| \_minOrderUsd | `uint256` | Minimum order in whole numeraire units, e.g. dollars (0: none). The constructor scales it<br />and the $0.10 bid cap by the numeraire's own `decimals()`, so neither can be mis-scaled. |
| \_assetPrecision | `uint8` | Decimal places of a whole asset token an order may trade (4: at least 0.0001 token). |

deployment to hand control to the intended fee recipient / governance address, which
then calls `acceptOwnership`.


```solidity
function acceptOwnership() external;
```

<a id="sweep-currency-address" />

### sweep

Sweep an accumulated balance of `currency` held by this hook to `to`.

<i>
  Between transactions the hook's raw balance holds only stranded funds or donations;
  fees belong to feeVault. Maker input is escrowed as ERC-6909
  claims in the PoolManager, and the transient native-deposit ledger is cleared at the
  end of every tx, so no per-order escrow lives in the hook's balance across calls.
</i>

```solidity
function sweep(Currency currency, address to) external onlyOwner;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| currency | `Currency` |  |
| to | `address` |  |

Surcharge a filler pays on top of the maker's minimum: none. The 0.02% trade fee comes
out of what each side receives instead (`AsyncFiller.tradeFee`).

```solidity
function calculatePoolFee(uint24, uint256) public pure virtual returns (uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \_ | `uint24` |  |
| \_ | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="executeorder-asyncorder-bytes" />

### executeOrder

Fill `order` in full. Must be called from an authorized executor (router) that has
already paid the filler's gross output within the same unlock: for ERC20 output via
`PoolManager.settleFor(hook)`, for native output by sending ETH to this hook.

```solidity
function executeOrder(AsyncOrder calldata order, bytes calldata data) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| data | `bytes` | abi.encode(filler) — the address that should receive the maker's input. |

<a id="flashfill-bytes" />

### flashFill

The hook's side of a Router flash fill, run by `MultiAsset.run`. `args` is
`abi.encode(uint8 op, AsyncOrder order, address filler)`: op 0 closes the order and credits its input,
less the trade fee, to `filler` as claims; 1 pays the maker of that open flash fill from the output claims
the Router has transferred here; 2 is a full fill paid in claims. Router only.

```solidity
function flashFill(bytes calldata args) external returns (uint256, uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| args | `bytes` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="matchneworder-asyncorder" />

### matchNewOrder

<a id="fillorderfrompoolliquidity-asyncorder-bytes32-uint160" />

### fillOrderFromPoolLiquidity

<i>
  The self-call boundary makes a failed AMM attempt atomic while preserving the resting
  order. PoolManager skips hook callbacks when the hook itself is the swap caller, so this
  swap does not create an order.
  `sqrtPriceLimitX96` is a price the swap may not cross (0 for none). Without one the whole order
  fills or the call reverts; with one the pool may fill part and leave the rest on the book.
</i>

```solidity
function fillOrderFromPoolLiquidity(AsyncOrder calldata order, bytes32 id, uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| sqrtPriceLimitX96 | `uint160` |  |

<a id="cancelorder-asyncorder" />

### cancelOrder

Maker cancels an unfilled order. Must be called via an authorized executor inside
an `IPoolManager.unlock` context. The executor must have asserted maker identity.

<i>
  The trusted Router needs no grant: it cancels only for `order.owner` or with the owner's signature,
  and a cancel only returns input to the owner, so revoking the Router never traps a maker's orders.
</i>

```solidity
function cancelOrder(AsyncOrder calldata order) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

<a id="_verifyreprice-asyncorder-bytes32-uint256-uint256-uint256-uint256-bytes" />

### \_verifyReprice

<i>
  Verifies a signed `UpdatePrice` against the order's creation sequence and reprice count, and returns
  its minimum for the order's live input: orders only shrink, so a live input above the signed one means
  the signature was for another order, and a smaller one gets the signed price, rounded up.
</i>

```solidity
function _verifyReprice(
        AsyncOrder calldata order,
        bytes32 id,
        uint256 amountIn,
        uint256 newAmountOutMin,
        uint256 nonce,
        uint256 deadline,
        bytes calldata signature
    ) private returns (uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| newAmountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| nonce | `uint256` |  |
| deadline | `uint256` |  |
| signature | `bytes` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="usenonce-address-uint256" />

### useNonce

Burns `maker`'s nonce for a signature the Router verified itself (`cancelWithSig`).
Every maker signature shares this one nonce space, so `invalidateNonce` revokes those
signatures too, and only the trusted Router may burn one: any other executor could
void the maker's signed actions on every pool.
The Router needs no grant here, so a maker who revoked it can still cancel by signature.

```solidity
function useNonce(address maker, uint256 nonce) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| maker | `address` |  |
| nonce | `uint256` |  |

<a id="receive" />

### receive

Accept ETH transfers. The Router (or any caller paying for a native-output
fill) forwards `msg.value` to the hook before triggering `executeOrder`. The hook
records the deposit on a transient slot so `executeOrder` settles only against the
filler's same-transaction deposit. ETH sent without a follow-up `executeOrder` stays
in the hook balance and is recoverable only through `sweep`.

```solidity
receive() external payable;
```

### PriorityFeeNeedsNumeraire

Priority bids are paid in the numeraire, so orders on a pool without it take no bid.

```solidity
error PriorityFeeNeedsNumeraire();
```

### CannotRevokeTrustedRouter

<i>
  Revoking the Router would strand the maker's live orders: Router.cancelOrder, cancelWithSig,
  fillOrder and fillFromPoolLiquidity all need the grant, and an EOA can't cancel from its own
  unlock. So the trusted Router can never be revoked; any other executor can.
</i>

```solidity
error CannotRevokeTrustedRouter();
```

## Structs

### UserParams

Hook params decoded from the `hookData` of `IPoolManager.swap`. The maker sets
`amountOutMin` (their limit price); `executor` is the address authorized to call fill.
Salt is contract-assigned at create time (see `_createOrder`) and emitted in
`AsyncOrderCreated` — the maker fetches it from the event log to reference the
order in cancel / updatePrice later.

```solidity
struct UserParams {
        address user;
        address executor;
        uint256 amountOutMin;
        uint256 priorityFee;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| user | `address` |  |
| executor | `address` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| priorityFee | `uint256` |  |

# MatchingEngine

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/MatchingEngine.sol)

**Title:** MatchingEngine

Standalone price-time matching harness. It maintains a radix-indexed
limit book and emits deterministic fill instructions.

<i>
  Algorithm and gas benchmark only: it does not custody or settle tokens.
  Live orders settle through the AsyncSwap hook and AsyncMatching.
</i>

## Constants

### PRICE_SCALE

```solidity
uint128 public constant PRICE_SCALE = 1e18;
```

### MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL

```solidity
uint8 public constant MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL = 8;
```

## State Variables

### books

```solidity
mapping(bytes32 market => Book) private books;
```

# NativeClaims

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/NativeClaims.sol)

Redeems the caller's PoolManager native ETH claims to a chosen recipient.

<i>

  Claim ownership and allowances are enforced by PoolManager.burn. No hook escrow is accessible.
</i>

# Router

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/Router.sol)

**Inherits:** EIP712, Multicall

**Title:** Router

**Author:** @msakiart

Thin entrypoint for makers (`swap`, `topUpPriorityFee`, `cancelOrder`, `cancelAndWithdraw`, `withdrawClaims`), fillers
(`fillOrder`) and keepers (`matchBook`, `fillFromPoolLiquidity`), batched with `multicall`. Each action
goes through `IPoolManager.unlock` so the hook can operate on PM debts. Native payouts/refunds are
PoolManager claims (ID 0), redeemable through NativeClaims or `withdrawClaims`; ERC20 payouts remain
direct.

Gasless variants (`swapWithSig`, `cancelWithSig`) take the maker's EIP-712 signature so a
relayer can submit. Signed creates pull input through Permit2 with the order as witness,
so the wallet shows the full order (tokens, amounts, pool) in one readable message.

`multicall` runs several of these as one atomic transaction, each as the caller (for example,
cancel many orders and withdraw the claims). It is not payable, so native-value actions
(`swap` with native input, `fillOrder` with native output) cannot reuse one `msg.value`.
Each action keeps its own PoolManager unlock and sets the transient slots it reads.

Order creation and fills (`swap`, `swapWithSig`, `fillOrder`, `fillFromPoolLiquidity`) pay an MEV tax
("Priority Is All You Need", Robinson & White): `mevTax()`, the transaction's priority fee per gas times
`MEV_TAX_GAS`, in ETH on top of any native deposit, credited to the FeeVault as native claims. On a chain
that orders by priority fee, searchers racing for the same position bid it up, so most of what they race
for goes to the protocol; a transaction with no priority pays nothing. Inside `multicall`, which is not
payable, a taxed action needs a transaction with no priority.
Flash fills (`fillOrderWithCallback`) charge the tax per fill as a PoolManager debt instead; see
`IAsyncSwapCallback`.

### POOLMANAGER

<a id="swap-asyncorder-bytes" />

### swap

Maker submits a new async order. `userData` must encode `AsyncSwap.UserParams`
with `executor == address(this)` so the router is authorized to fill later.
`userData.amountOutMin` MUST equal `order.amountOutMin` — the router enforces
this so the limit price the maker signs in `order` is exactly what beforeSwap
stores via hookData.

The hook auto-assigns a salt on create and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated`.
Submitters can pass `order.salt = bytes32(0)` on initial submission; the
field is only read on cancel / updatePrice / fill paths (where the maker
supplies the salt fetched from the indexer or event log).

Native input (currency0 = address(0) and zeroForOne = true, OR currency1 =
address(0) and zeroForOne = false) requires `msg.value == order.amountIn` —
the router holds the ETH and settles it to PM during unlock. For ERC20 input
the maker must approve the router for `amountIn` of the input token. Either way `msg.value`
also carries the MEV tax (`mevTax()`, zero without a priority fee).

```solidity
function swap(AsyncOrder calldata order, bytes memory userData) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| userData | `bytes` |  |

<a id="fillorder-asyncorder-uint256-bytes" />

### fillOrder

Filler completes an open order, paying exactly the maker's live minimum. The maker
receives it less the 0.02% trade fee, and the filler the input less 0.02%.
For ERC20 output, approve the router for that amount. For native output,
`msg.value` must equal the live minimum;
a stale or excessive deposit reverts rather than stranding the difference. `msg.value`
also carries the MEV tax (`mevTax()`, zero without a priority fee).
Native output is currency1 for zeroForOne, otherwise currency0.

`maxPrice` caps the output the filler pays —
it protects fillers from a maker who front-runs them with `updatePrice` to
bump the order's stored price. Pass `type(uint256).max` to disable the check.
`order.amountIn` is the least input the filler accepts: the fill reverts if the
order's live input has dropped below it (e.g. after a partial match).

```solidity
function fillOrder(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |
| \_ | `bytes` |  |

<a id="swapwithsig-asyncorder-permitdata-executorgrant" />

### swapWithSig

Relayer submits a maker's signed order. The maker signs a Permit2
`PermitWitnessTransferFrom` for `amountIn` of the input token with `spender = Router`
and the `AsyncOrder` witness (see `OrderSignatures`), so one signature both approves
the transfer and commits to the order. Input then lands in the hook escrow exactly as
in `swap`. Requires a prior Permit2 approval of the input token; native input is not
supported (use `swap`). The relayer pays the MEV tax for its transaction's priority in `msg.value`.

```solidity
function swapWithSig(AsyncOrder calldata order, PermitData calldata permit, ExecutorGrant calldata grant)
        external
        payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| permit | `PermitData` |  |
| grant | `ExecutorGrant` |  |

<a id="topuppriorityfee-asyncorder-uint256" />

### topUpPriorityFee

Add `addedFee` numeraire units to the caller's remaining priority bid.

<i>
  Requires an ERC20 approval to this Router. Leaves amount and price unchanged and resets
  fee-tier FIFO age. No matching or MEV tax; use multicall with matchBook to attempt matching.
  Only the order's identity fields are used; addedFee is a delta, not a target total.
</i>

<a id="_settlewithpermit-currency-asyncorder-permitdata" />

### \_settleWithPermit

<i>

# RouterFlashFills

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/RouterFlashFills.sol)

**Inherits:** [IAsyncSwapCallback](/reference/src/interfaces/IAsyncSwapCallback)

**Title:** RouterFlashFills

**Author:** @msakiart

The Router's flash-fill surface (`IAsyncSwapCallback`). The Router creates this module in its constructor
and runs it by DELEGATECALL from its `fallback`, so every call executes as the Router: the hook sees the
Router as caller, and the transient filler slot lives in the Router's context. Kept out of the Router so
its runtime stays under EIP-170.

<i>
  Called directly (not through the Router) every hook call reverts `NotTrustedRouter`.
</i>

## Constants

### POOLMANAGER

```solidity
IPoolManager immutable POOLMANAGER;
```

### HOOK

```solidity
AsyncSwap immutable HOOK;
```

### MEV_TAX_GAS

```solidity
uint256 immutable MEV_TAX_GAS;
```

### FLASH_FILLER_LOCATION

<i>
  Router transient slot this module shares (see Router).
  keccak256("Router.FlashFiller") - 1: the filler of the flash fill in progress, zero otherwise.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant FLASH_FILLER_LOCATION = 0x8a32db0797977fc7694da75ada74debc8ae08fbf3557ccd5133e780e8ba11369;
```

### FLASH_FILL_ACTION

<i>
  First word of the Router's unlock data for a flash fill: `Router.ActionType.FlashFill`.
</i>

```solidity
uint8 constant FLASH_FILL_ACTION = 9;
```

### BEGIN

```solidity
uint8 constant BEGIN = 0;
```

### SETTLE

```solidity
uint8 constant SETTLE = 1;
```

### FILL

```solidity
uint8 constant FILL = 2;
```

<a id="fillorderwithcallback-asyncorder-uint256-bytes" />

### fillOrderWithCallback

Fill `order` with no inventory: input first as claims, callback, then the owed output as claims.
Every fill in the callback (this one and each `fillOrderInCallback`) owes the MEV tax, paid to the
FeeVault when the fill runs. `msg.value` prepays it, any amount; the filler may also pay inside its
callback with `PoolManager.settleFor(router)`. A surplus is returned to the filler in ETH and a
shortfall reverts `MevTaxUnpaid`.

```solidity
function fillOrderWithCallback(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata data) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |
| data | `bytes` |  |

<a id="unlockcallback-bytes" />

### unlockCallback

Body of a flash fill: the Router's `unlockCallback` forwards its calldata here (running as the Router)
when the action is a flash fill. Input first, callback, then the output check and payout.

```solidity
function unlockCallback(bytes calldata data) external returns (bytes memory);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| data | `bytes` |  |

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes` |  |

<a id="mevtaxfor-uint256" />

<a id="mevtaxowed" />

### mevTaxOwed

<a id="_checkfill-asyncorder-uint256" />

### \_checkFill

<i>
  Checks the live order against the filler's bounds and returns the output owed: the live minimum, at most
  `maxPrice`, for a live input of at least `order.amountIn`. A missing order is left for the hook to reject.
  The flash path charges no pool fee, so the hook burns exactly the live minimum it returns.
  A Dutch auction order is stepped first, so the filler pays the scheduled price, not an older one.
</i>

```solidity
function _checkFill(AsyncOrder memory order, uint256 maxPrice) private returns (uint256 livePrice);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| livePrice | `uint256` |  |

# TokenClaims

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/TokenClaims.sol)

Redeems the caller's PoolManager currency claims to a chosen recipient.

<i>
  Approve this contract for the currency claim ID on PoolManager before redeeming.
  Claim ownership and allowances are enforced by PoolManager.burn. No hook escrow is accessible.
</i>

<a id="afteraddliquidity-address-poolkey-modifyliquidityparams-balancedelta-balancedelta-bytes" />

### afterAddLiquidity

The hook called after liquidity is added

```solidity
function afterAddLiquidity(
        address sender,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        ModifyLiquidityParams calldata params,
        BalanceDelta delta,
        BalanceDelta feesAccrued,
        bytes calldata hookData
    ) external onlyPoolManager returns (bytes4, BalanceDelta);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| sender | `address` | The initial msg.sender for the add liquidity call |
| key | `PoolKey` | The key for the pool |
| params | `ModifyLiquidityParams` | The parameters for adding liquidity |
| delta | `BalanceDelta` | The caller's balance delta after adding liquidity; the sum of principal delta, fees accrued, and hook delta |
| feesAccrued | `BalanceDelta` | The fees accrued since the last time fees were collected from this position |
| hookData | `bytes` | Arbitrary data handed into the PoolManager by the liquidity provider to be passed on to the hook |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes4` | bytes4 The function selector for the hook |
| \<none> | `BalanceDelta` | BalanceDelta The hook's delta in token0 and token1. Positive: the hook is owed/took currency, negative: the hook owes/sent currency |

| params | `ModifyLiquidityParams` | The parameters for removing liquidity |
| delta | `BalanceDelta` | The caller's balance delta after removing liquidity; the sum of principal delta, fees accrued, and hook delta |
| feesAccrued | `BalanceDelta` | The fees accrued since the last time fees were collected from this position |
| hookData | `bytes` | Arbitrary data handed into the PoolManager by the liquidity provider to be be passed on to the hook |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes4` | bytes4 The function selector for the hook |
| \<none> | `BalanceDelta` | BalanceDelta The hook's delta in token0 and token1. Positive: the hook is owed/took currency, negative: the hook owes/sent currency |

<a id="_afterremoveliquidity-address-poolkey-modifyliquidityparams-balancedelta-balancedelta-bytes" />

# IAsyncSwapCallback

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/interfaces/IAsyncSwapCallback.sol)

**Title:** IAsyncSwapCallback

The Router's callback fill surface: `fillOrderWithCallback` opens a fill and calls the filler back
(`IAsyncSwapFlashFiller.asyncSwapFlashFill`); the `...InCallback` functions are the only Router calls
accepted while that callback runs, and only from its filler. Every other Router entry point reverts
`FlashFillActive` until the callback returns.

## Functions

<a id="fillorderwithcallback-asyncorder-uint256-bytes" />

### fillOrderWithCallback

Fill `order` with no inventory: input first as claims, callback, then the owed output as claims.
Every fill in the callback (this one and each `fillOrderInCallback`) owes the MEV tax, paid to the
FeeVault when the fill runs. `msg.value` prepays it, any amount; the filler may also pay inside its
callback with `PoolManager.settleFor(router)`. A surplus is returned to the filler in ETH and a
shortfall reverts `MevTaxUnpaid`.

```solidity
function fillOrderWithCallback(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata data) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |
| data | `bytes` |  |

<a id="fillorderincallback-asyncorder-uint256" />

### fillOrderInCallback

Inside the callback: fill another open order, paying its output and receiving its input as claims.

```solidity
function fillOrderInCallback(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |

<a id="matchbookincallback-poolkey-uint8" />

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

<a id="mevtaxfor-uint256" />

### mevTaxFor

MEV tax for `fills` fills at this transaction's priority fee. Off chain, simulate with the gas price
you will send (`eth_call` with `gasPrice`); on chain it is exact for the running transaction.

```solidity
function mevTaxFor(uint256 fills) external view returns (uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| fills | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="mevtaxowed" />

### mevTaxOwed

Inside the callback: the MEV tax the Router still owes for this flash fill, every fill charged so far
less what was paid. Settle exactly this with `PoolManager.settleFor(router)` before returning.

```solidity
function mevTaxOwed() external view returns (uint256);
```

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

# IAsyncSwapFlashFiller

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/interfaces/IAsyncSwapFlashFiller.sol)

**Title:** IAsyncSwapFlashFiller

Callback a filler contract implements to use `Router.flashFill`.

## Functions

<a id="asyncswapflashfill-asyncorder-uint256-uint256-bytes" />

### asyncSwapFlashFill

Called by the Router inside its PoolManager unlock, after the order was closed and its input,
less the 0.02% trade fee, credited to the filler as ERC-6909 claims (`amountIn` of the input
currency, id 0 for native ETH).

<i>
  Before returning, the filler must hold `amountOwed` claims of the order's output currency and allow
  the Router to transfer them (`PoolManager.approve(router, id, amountOwed)` or an operator grant). Inside
  the callback it may swap on any v4 pool, `burn`/`mint`/`take`/`settle`, and fill other Async Swap orders
  through `IAsyncSwapCallback.fillOrderInCallback` and `matchBookInCallback`. Every delta it opens must be zero
  when the Router's unlock ends.
</i>

```solidity
function asyncSwapFlashFill(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOwed, bytes calldata data)
        external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOwed | `uint256` |  |
| data | `bytes` |  |

# ISignatureTransfer

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/interfaces/ISignatureTransfer.sol)

**Title:** ISignatureTransfer

Minimal subset of Uniswap Permit2's SignatureTransfer interface used by the Router.
Canonical Permit2 lives at 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 on every chain.

<i>
  Vendored instead of imported because Permit2's sources pin solc 0.8.17.
</i>

# AsyncFiller

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol)

**Title:** AsyncFiller

**Author:** @msakiart

Stores open async orders and settles fills against them.

<i>
  Authorization model: the maker authorizes a Router/executor at order-creation time
  (`setExecutor[owner][executor] = true`). All subsequent fill / cancel / updatePrice
  calls on the hook must come from that registered executor. The hook forwards its
  immediate caller (`msg.sender`) and the resolved end-actor address (filler / canceller)
  into this library; the executor is checked here, and PM settlement targets the actor.
</i>

## Constants

### MAX_PRIORITY_FEE

```solidity
uint64 internal constant MAX_PRIORITY_FEE = type(uint64).max;
```

### MIN_PRIORITY_FEE

<i>
  Default $0.10 cap for six-decimal numeraires. A pool may override this for other decimals.
</i>

```solidity
uint64 internal constant MIN_PRIORITY_FEE = 100_000;
```

### PRIORITY_FEE_BPS

<i>
  Below a $100 order the least bid is 10 bps of the order instead: min($0.10, 0.1% of it).
</i>

```solidity
uint256 internal constant PRIORITY_FEE_BPS = 10;
```

### TRADE_FEE_BPS

<i>
  Protocol fee on what each side of a book match or filler fill receives: 0.02%.
</i>

```solidity
uint256 internal constant TRADE_FEE_BPS = 2;
```

### NO_PRIORITY_BIDS

<i>
  `Book.priorityFeeCap` of a pool without the numeraire: bids are paid in the numeraire, so it takes none.
</i>

```solidity
uint64 internal constant NO_PRIORITY_BIDS = type(uint64).max;
```

<a id="checkminimum-book-bool-uint256-uint256" />

### checkMinimum

Reverts unless the order's numeraire leg is at least the pool's minimum (a buy's input, a
sell's minimum output) and its asset leg at least the pool's asset floor (a sell's input, a buy's minimum
output). Neither reads the pool price, which whoever initializes the pool sets.

```solidity
function checkMinimum(Book storage book, bool isBuy, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMin) internal view;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| book | `Book` |  |
| isBuy | `bool` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |

<a id="fill-state-book-asyncorder-bytes32-address-address-address-address-uint256" />

### fill

Full-fill. The caller (the hook contract) must be an authorized executor of the
order owner; `filler` is the actual end-user paying the output and receiving the
input. Must be invoked from inside an `IPoolManager.unlock` context.

<i>
  Settle gross output (native only; ERC20 is pre-settled), pay the signed minimum less the trade fee to the
  maker, and mint fee claims to the vault. Burn input claims and pay the input less the trade fee to the
  filler. Both currency deltas net to zero. A failed fill reverts all legs.
</i>

```solidity
function fill(
        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        address executor,
        address filler,
        address feeVault,
        uint256 fee
    ) internal;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `State` |  |
| book | `Book` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| hook | `address` |  |
| executor | `address` |  |
| filler | `address` |  |
| feeVault | `address` |  |
| fee | `uint256` |  |

<a id="beginflashfill-state-book-asyncorder-bytes32-address-address" />

### beginFlashFill

Input-first half of a flash fill, run in the hook's context. Closes the order (so it cannot be
repriced, cancelled, topped up, matched or filled again) and credits its escrowed input, less the trade
fee, to `filler` as ERC-6909 claims. Returns the order's input and minimum output as they were.

<i>
  The caller must then call `settleClaimsOutput` in the same unlock, after the hook has received the output
  as claims; otherwise the unlock cannot close and the whole fill reverts.
</i>

```solidity
function beginFlashFill(
        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address executor,
        address filler
    ) internal returns (uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOutMin);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `State` |  |
| book | `Book` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| executor | `address` |  |
| filler | `address` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |

<a id="settleclaimsoutput-state-asyncorder-bytes32-address-uint256-uint256" />

### settleClaimsOutput

Output half of a fill paid in claims, run in the hook's context: burns `amountOutMin` of the hook's
output claims (which the Router has just transferred to it), pays the maker the minimum less the trade
fee and the vault the fee. The order must already be closed.

```solidity
function settleClaimsOutput(
        State storage self,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address filler,
        uint256 amountIn,
        uint256 amountOutMin
    ) internal;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `State` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| filler | `address` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |

<a id="cancel-state-book-asyncorder-bytes32-address-address" />

### cancel

Cancel an unfilled order. Must be called inside an unlock context. Auth: `executor`
must be either the order owner themselves (smart-contract makers calling the hook
directly from their own unlock) or an executor the maker authorised via
`setExecutor`. Funds always return to `order.owner`.

```solidity

        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        address executor
    ) internal;
```

## Structs

### OrderInfo

Open-order record. Filler fills are full-order; direct matches can reduce it
partially while keeping the remaining input in escrow.

```solidity
struct OrderInfo {
        address owner;
        uint256 amountIn;
        uint256 amountOutMin;
        uint128 price;
        bool isBuy;
        bool zeroForOne;
        uint64 sequence;
        /// @dev Maker reprices so far; signed reprices commit to it (`OrderSignatures.hashUpdatePrice`).
        uint32 reprices;
        /// @dev The bid, escrowed as hook claims since the order was created.
        uint64 priorityFee;
        uint128 priorityKey;
        /// @dev Immutable settlement age; repricing only resets queue sequence.
        uint64 createdSequence;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| owner | `address` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| price | `uint128` |  |
| isBuy | `bool` |  |
| zeroForOne | `bool` |  |
| sequence | `uint64` |  |
| reprices | `uint32` |  |
| priorityFee | `uint64` |  |
| priorityKey | `uint128` |  |
| createdSequence | `uint64` |  |

```solidity
        mapping(uint32 nodeId => EligiblePrice.Ratio) exactBounds;
```

```solidity
struct State {

        address feeVault;

        mapping(address owner => mapping(address executor => bool)) isExecutor;

        uint64 refBlock;
    }
```

### Book

```solidity
struct Book {
        uint64 nextSequence;
        uint64 openOrderCount;
        /// @dev $0.10 in this pool's numeraire base units. Zero uses the six-decimal default.
        uint64 priorityFeeCap;
        TickBitmap.Tree bids;
        TickBitmap.Tree asks;
        mapping(uint128 price => PriceLevel) bidLevels;
        mapping(uint128 price => PriceLevel) askLevels;
        /// @dev Least order size in numeraire base units (0: none); see `checkMinimum`.
        uint256 minOrder;
        /// @dev Least asset amount an order may trade, from the asset's decimals and the hook's precision.
        uint256 minAssetAmount;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| nextSequence | `uint64` |  |
| openOrderCount | `uint64` |  |
| priorityFeeCap | `uint64` |  |
| bids | `TickBitmap.Tree` |  |
| asks | `TickBitmap.Tree` |  |
| bidLevels | `mapping(uint128 price => PriceLevel)` |  |
| askLevels | `mapping(uint128 price => PriceLevel)` |  |
| minOrder | `uint256` |  |
| minAssetAmount | `uint256` |  |

# AsyncMatching

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol)

Linked matching module operating on the hook's order and radix-book storage.

<i>
  Public library calls use DELEGATECALL, so ERC-6909 escrow remains owned by Async Swap.
</i>

## Constants

### MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL

```solidity
uint8 public constant MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL = 8;
```

### POOL_LIQUIDITY_FILL_FEE

<i>
  LP fee on a pool-liquidity fill, in v4 pips: 0.02%.
</i>

```solidity
uint24 private constant POOL_LIQUIDITY_FILL_FEE = 200;
```

<a id="fillfrompoolliquidity-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-poolkey-bytes32-address-uint160" />

### fillFromPoolLiquidity

Execute an order against active v4 LP positions if they meet the signed minimum.

<i>
  Reverts atomically on insufficient liquidity or output; the caller catches this across a self-call so
  the resting order is preserved. Without a price limit the whole order must fill. With one (the best
  book level, when the pool goes first) the swap may stop there: the filled part must meet the maker's
  limit pro rata, and the rest stays on the book with the maker's own limit for the book to match.
</i>

```solidity
function fillFromPoolLiquidity(
        AsyncFiller.State storage self,
        AsyncFiller.Book storage book,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96
    ) public;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| book | `AsyncFiller.Book` |  |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| hook | `address` |  |
| sqrtPriceLimitX96 | `uint160` |  |

<a id="_reduceafterpoolfill-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-poolkey-bytes32-uint256" />

<a id="_poolfillnet-asyncfiller-state-poolkey-bytes32-address-uint160" />

### \_poolFillNet

<i>
  Swap the order's input less the protocol's 0.01% (rounded up, paid to the vault), then take the dynamic
  fee (`DynamicFeeOrdering`) from the output. A swap stopped short at `sqrtPriceLimitX96` pays the 0.01% on
  what it swapped. Returns the input swapped, the input used including the 0.01%, and the net output,
  reverting unless the output meets the maker's limit on the input used.
</i>

```solidity
function _poolFillNet(
        AsyncFiller.State storage self,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        uint160 sqrtPriceLimitX96
    ) private returns (uint256 swapped, uint256 consumed, uint256 amountOut);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| hook | `address` |  |
| sqrtPriceLimitX96 | `uint160` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| swapped | `uint256` |  |
| consumed | `uint256` |  |
| amountOut | `uint256` |  |

<a id="_chargefees-asyncfiller-state-poolkey-bytes32-uint256-int24-uint256" />

### \_chargeFees

<i>
  Pay the 0.01% from the input's escrow to the vault and charge the dynamic fee on the output; returns
  the dynamic fee.
</i>

```solidity
        AsyncFiller.State storage self,

        int24 tickBefore,

    ) private returns (uint256);
```

<a id="_crosses-uint128-uint128-asyncfiller-orderinfo-asyncfiller-orderinfo" />

### \_crosses

Decide whether a buy and a sell order cross, i.e. a price exists that satisfies both
makers' limits.

<i>
  Keys are the floor ticks of the exact limits, ordered by numeraire per asset, so two
  distinct prices can share a key. Strictly ordered keys decide the result directly,
  since a monotone key cannot invert a strict inequality. Equal keys are decided by a
  full-precision cross-multiply:
</i>

cross  \<=>  buyIn/buyOut >= sellOut/sellIn  \<=>  buyIn*sellIn >= sellOut*buyOut
\<=>  floor(buyIn\*sellIn / sellOut) >= buyOut   (sellOut, buyOut are nonzero).

An exact tie counts as a cross. With equal keys the quotient is on the order of
`buyOut`, so the `mulDiv` cannot overflow for escrowable amounts.

```solidity
function _crosses(
        uint128 buyKey,
        uint128 sellKey,
        AsyncFiller.OrderInfo storage buy,
        AsyncFiller.OrderInfo storage sell
    ) internal view returns (bool);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| buyKey | `uint128` |  |
| sellKey | `uint128` |  |
| buy | `AsyncFiller.OrderInfo` |  |
| sell | `AsyncFiller.OrderInfo` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bool` |  |

# DutchAuction

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/DutchAuction.sol)

**Title:** DutchAuction

**Author:** @msakiart

Linked module for Dutch auction orders. The maker of a resting order sets a floor and a duration in blocks,
and the order's minimum output then falls in a straight line from its price at start to the floor. Anyone
may call `step` to write the scheduled minimum into the order, by the same reprice path a maker uses, so
the book always holds a real price. The Router steps the order before every filler fill.

<i>
  Between steps the stored minimum is at or above the schedule, so the maker never receives less than the
  schedule gives. A maker reprice stops the auction: `step` sees a reprice count it did not write.
  Public library calls use DELEGATECALL, so the auctions and books stay in the hook.
</i>

## Constants

### MAX_DURATION

Longest auction, in blocks.

```solidity
uint32 internal constant MAX_DURATION = 50_000;
```

## Functions

<a id="start-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-mapping-bytes32-auction-asyncorder-bytes32-uint256-uint32-address" />

### start

Start an auction on a resting order. Maker only. The order's current minimum is the start price.

```solidity
function start(
        AsyncFiller.State storage self,
        AsyncFiller.Book storage book,
        mapping(bytes32 => Auction) storage auctions,
        AsyncOrder calldata order,
        bytes32 id,
        uint256 floorAmountOutMin,
        uint32 duration,
        address caller
    ) public;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| book | `AsyncFiller.Book` |  |
| auctions | `mapping(bytes32 => Auction)` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| floorAmountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| duration | `uint32` |  |
| caller | `address` |  |

<a id="step-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-mapping-bytes32-auction-asyncorder-bytes32" />

Write the scheduled minimum into the order when it is below the stored one. Anyone may call it.

# DynamicFeeOrdering

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/DynamicFeeOrdering.sol)

**Title:** Dynamic fee ordering on pool-liquidity fills

Linked library called by `AsyncMatching` in the hook's context.

## Constants

### ORDERING_WINDOW

<i>
  Blocks a pool fill's starting tick stays the reference that later fills are measured against.
</i>

```solidity
uint256 internal constant ORDERING_WINDOW = 2;
```

## Functions

<a id="charge-asyncfiller-state-poolkey-bytes32-currency-int24-uint256" />

### charge

<i>
  Dynamic fee on a pool fill that backruns a price move, taken from its output. The first pool fill in a window of
  `ORDERING_WINDOW` blocks records its starting tick as the reference. A later fill in the
  window that moves the price back toward the reference pays half the price gap it closes:
  `amountOut * avgGap / 2`, with the gap averaged over the fill's start and end ticks (one
  tick is about 0.01%), so splitting a backrun does not lower its total. A fill that crosses
  the reference pays only on the share of its output from the side before the reference,
  in proportion to the ticks on each side. Half of the fee
  is donated to in-range LPs and half credited to the FeeVault as claims.
</i>

```solidity
function charge(
        AsyncFiller.State storage self,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        bytes32 id,
        Currency output,
        int24 tickBefore,
        uint256 amountOut
    ) public returns (uint256 fee);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| output | `Currency` |  |
| tickBefore | `int24` |  |
| amountOut | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| fee | `uint256` |  |

<a id="_pay-asyncfiller-state-poolkey-bytes32-currency-uint256" />

### \_pay

<i>
  Half of `fee` to in-range LPs (all of it to the FeeVault if none are in range), the rest
  to the FeeVault as claims.
</i>

```solidity
function _pay(AsyncFiller.State storage self, PoolKey calldata key, bytes32 id, Currency output, uint256 fee)
        private;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| output | `Currency` |  |
| fee | `uint256` |  |

</i>

| observedBlock | `uint64` |  |

# EligiblePrice

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/EligiblePrice.sol)

Exact-price summaries on a priority-key radix tree.

<i>
  A buy subtree stores its maximum limit; a sell subtree its minimum.
  This is an existence certificate, not an approximation of an order's limit.
</i>

## Functions

<a id="le-ratio-ratio" />

### le

<i>
  Exact comparison of positive-denominator ratios using two 512-bit products.
</i>

```solidity
function le(Ratio memory a, Ratio memory b) internal pure returns (bool result);
```

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| a | `Ratio` |  |

| Name | Type | Description |

| result | `bool` |  |

# IncomingMatching

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/IncomingMatching.sol)

Fund a crossing arrival, match it in memory, then index only its remainder.

<i>
  Active LP pools retain the existing storage path. Pending orders cannot match before funding.
</i>

# MultiAsset

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/MultiAsset.sol)

**Title:** MultiAsset

**Author:** @msakiart

Linked module for multi-asset trading: pool setup (including pools without the numeraire) and the hook's
side of flash fills and of fills paid in ERC-6909 claims. Public library calls use DELEGATECALL, so escrow,
books and the transient flash record stay in the hook.

## Constants

### BEGIN

Close the order and credit its input, less the trade fee, to the filler as claims; record it as the
open flash fill. Returns the input credited and the output owed.

```solidity
uint8 internal constant BEGIN = 0;
```

### SETTLE

Pay the maker of the open flash fill out of the output claims the Router has transferred to the hook.

```solidity
uint8 internal constant SETTLE = 1;
```

### FILL

A full fill paid in claims (inside a flash fill): the hook already holds the output as claims.

```solidity
uint8 internal constant FILL = 2;
```

### FLASH_ORDER_SLOT

<i>
  Transient record of the open flash fill, in the hook's context: its id, then the input and minimum output
  it was opened at. Each slot is keccak256("asyncswap.flashFill.\<name>") - 1.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 private constant FLASH_ORDER_SLOT = 0xadcc9340e9b9520481a90c5e1cb2c7bb827085ef7c7b209a028db0fe766510cd;
```

### FLASH_AMOUNT_IN_SLOT

```solidity
bytes32 private constant FLASH_AMOUNT_IN_SLOT = 0xa948fdbbf716a51dd3ab76f9643ccf5ff5ac531fed11e84d483629e540b40220;
```

### FLASH_AMOUNT_OUT_SLOT

```solidity
bytes32 private constant FLASH_AMOUNT_OUT_SLOT = 0x4af24310f6994917e24875d474455b553ed83a7345f90cd7dd124597d7de6b85;
```

## Functions

<a id="initialize-mapping-poolid-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-poolkey-poolconfig" />

### initialize

Set up a new pool's state and book. Anyone may open a pool that pairs the numeraire with a dynamic fee. A
pool without the numeraire (for example ETH/TOKEN) may be opened only once both of its tokens have a
numeraire pool on this hook with the same tick spacing, so every such order has a numeraire route for
fillers. On it `currency1` is the quote side, each side's minimum is its token's decimal floor (no dollar
minimum), and priority bids are refused (`AsyncFiller.NO_PRIORITY_BIDS`). No check reads a price.

```solidity
function initialize(
        mapping(PoolId => AsyncFiller.State) storage states,
        AsyncFiller.Book storage book,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        PoolConfig calldata config
    ) public;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| states | `mapping(PoolId => AsyncFiller.State)` |  |
| book | `AsyncFiller.Book` |  |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| config | `PoolConfig` |  |

<a id="_requirenumerairepool-mapping-poolid-asyncfiller-state-currency-currency-int24" />

### \_requireNumerairePool

<i>
  Reverts `NumeraireRequired` unless `currency` already has a numeraire pool on this hook with `tickSpacing`.
</i>

```solidity
function _requireNumerairePool(
        mapping(PoolId => AsyncFiller.State) storage states,
        Currency numeraire,
        Currency currency,
        int24 tickSpacing
    ) private view;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| states | `mapping(PoolId => AsyncFiller.State)` |  |
| numeraire | `Currency` |  |
| currency | `Currency` |  |
| tickSpacing | `int24` |  |

<a id="_minassetamount-currency-uint8" />

### \_minAssetAmount

<i>
  10^(decimals - assetPrecision) base units of `asset`, at least 1. Native ETH has 18 decimals. A token
  without a readable `decimals()` gets the 1-unit floor, and reported decimals are capped at 36. An asset
  with no code reverts: a pool opened before its token is deployed would otherwise keep a 1-unit floor.
</i>

```solidity
function _minAssetAmount(Currency asset, uint8 assetPrecision) private view returns (uint256);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| asset | `Currency` |  |
| assetPrecision | `uint8` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="run-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-bytes-address" />

### run

<i>
  The flash path charges no pool fee: `AsyncSwap.calculatePoolFee` is zero, and the 0.02% trade fee comes
  out of what each side receives, as in a plain fill. `executor` is the hook's caller (the Router).
</i>

```solidity

        public

```

# OrderSignatures

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/OrderSignatures.sol)

**Title:** OrderSignatures

**Author:** @msakiart

EIP-712 types for signed AsyncSwap actions. Every type spells out the maker, both tokens
and the amounts so wallets render a readable message instead of opaque calldata.

* `AsyncOrder` is the Permit2 witness for `Router.swapWithSig` (Permit2 domain).
* `SetExecutor` and `UpdatePrice` are verified by the hook (AsyncSwap domain).
* `CancelOrder` is verified by the Router (AsyncSwap Router domain).

## Constants

### POOL_KEY_TYPE

```solidity
bytes internal constant POOL_KEY_TYPE =
        "PoolKey(address currency0,address currency1,uint24 fee,int24 tickSpacing,address hooks)";
```

### ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE

```solidity
bytes internal constant ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE =
        "AsyncOrder(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 amountOutMin,uint256 priorityFee,PoolKey pool)";
```

### POOL_KEY_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant POOL_KEY_TYPEHASH = keccak256(POOL_KEY_TYPE);
```

### ASYNC_ORDER_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant ASYNC_ORDER_TYPEHASH = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE, POOL_KEY_TYPE));
```

### PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE

Witness type string appended by Permit2 to `PermitWitnessTransferFrom(...)`.
Referenced types are sorted alphabetically per EIP-712.

```solidity
string internal constant PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE = string(
        abi.encodePacked(
            "AsyncOrder witness)", ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE, POOL_KEY_TYPE, "TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)"
        )
    );
```

### SET_EXECUTOR_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant SET_EXECUTOR_TYPEHASH = keccak256(
        abi.encodePacked(
            "SetExecutor(address maker,address executor,bool allow,PoolKey pool,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)",
            POOL_KEY_TYPE
        )
    );
```

### UPDATE_PRICE_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant UPDATE_PRICE_TYPEHASH = keccak256(
        "UpdatePrice(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 newAmountOutMin,bytes32 orderId,uint64 createdSequence,uint32 reprices,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)"
    );
```

### CANCEL_ORDER_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant CANCEL_ORDER_TYPEHASH = keccak256(
        "CancelOrder(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,bytes32 orderId,uint64 createdSequence,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)"
    );
```

## Functions

<a id="tokens-asyncorder" />

### tokens

```solidity
function tokens(AsyncOrder memory order) internal pure returns (address tokenIn, address tokenOut);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

# RadixPriceTree

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/RadixPriceTree.sol)

Patricia radix index for uint128 price levels. Inserts and removals
traverse at most 128 branch bits; each distinct price creates one
leaf and at most one branch node. Node ids released by `remove` are
recycled by later inserts, so the id counter only grows with the peak
number of simultaneously stored prices and can never be exhausted in
practice (2^31 simultaneous levels).

## Functions

<a id="insert-tree-uint128" />

### insert

```solidity
function insert(Tree storage self, uint128 price) internal returns (bool created);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `Tree` |  |
| price | `uint128` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| created | `bool` |  |

<a id="remove-tree-uint128" />

### remove

```solidity
function remove(Tree storage self, uint128 price) internal;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `Tree` |  |
| price | `uint128` |  |

<a id="best-tree-bool" />

### best

```solidity
function best(Tree storage self, bool highest) internal view returns (bool found, uint128 price);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `Tree` |  |
| highest | `bool` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| found | `bool` |  |
| price | `uint128` |  |

<a id="_newnode-tree" />

### \_newNode

<i>
  Reuse a released id first; only grow the counter when none is free. A freed id
  is referenced by nothing (its parent, sibling and `leaves` entries were rewired in
  `remove`), so reusing it cannot alias a live node.
</i>

```solidity

```
