# TickPrice

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/libraries/TickPrice.sol)

Book levels on Uniswap v4 ticks: an order sits at the floor tick (spacing 1, 0.01% steps)
of its exact currency1/currency0 limit. Levels are a fixed relative width at any price and
for any token decimals; the exact limit still decides crossing within a level.

## Functions

<a id="key-bool-bool-uint256-uint256" />

### key

Radix key of an order's level, ordered by numeraire per asset. Monotone in the exact
price, so distinct keys order prices strictly. Keys run from 1 to 2 \* MAX_TICK + 1;
ratios beyond the v4 price range share the end keys.

```solidity
function key(bool isBuy, bool zeroForOne, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOut) public pure returns (uint128);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| isBuy | `bool` |  |
| zeroForOne | `bool` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOut | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint128` |  |

<a id="poolbeatslevel-ipoolmanager-poolid-bool-bool-uint128-int24-uint64" />

### poolBeatsLevel

Whether the pool has active liquidity and its current price is strictly better for an
incoming order than the best opposite level `levelKey` (below the best ask for a buy,
above the best bid for a sell), compared as keys; if so, also the limit a pool-first swap
may not cross. `quote1`: the numeraire is currency1, so the tick's price is already
numeraire per asset; otherwise it is flipped.

<i>
  Inside the dynamic-fee window (`refTick`, `refBlock`; see `DynamicFeeOrdering`) a fill back toward the
  reference pays about half the price gap it closes, so the pool's price counts that much worse: half the
  gap, in ticks. The limit is the level's tick, one tick higher for a swap that lowers the tick (the key is
  a floor tick, so the floor would trade past the level's exact price), kept inside the range v4 accepts.
</i>

```solidity
function poolBeatsLevel(
        IPoolManager manager,
        PoolId poolId,
        bool quote1,
        bool isBuy,
        uint128 levelKey,
        int24 refTick,
        uint64 refBlock
    ) public view returns (bool, uint160);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| manager | `IPoolManager` |  |
| poolId | `PoolId` |  |
| quote1 | `bool` |  |
| isBuy | `bool` |  |
| levelKey | `uint128` |  |
| refTick | `int24` |  |
| refBlock | `uint64` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bool` |  |
| \<none> | `uint160` |  |

<a id="floortick-uint256-uint256" />

### floorTick

Largest tick whose price is at most num/den, clamped to the v4 tick range. Monotone in
num/den. Two regimes keep sqrt(num/den) \* 2^96 well inside one tick of exact.

```solidity
function floorTick(uint256 num, uint256 den) internal pure returns (int24);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| num | `uint256` |  |
| den | `uint256` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `int24` |  |

# AsyncSwapFlashFiller

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/periphery/AsyncSwapFlashFiller.sol)

**Inherits:** [IAsyncSwapFlashFiller](/reference/src/interfaces/IAsyncSwapFlashFiller)

**Title:** AsyncSwapFlashFiller

Base for flash fillers. Write `_route`; this contract handles the rest:

* only the Router may call the callback, and only for a fill this contract started;
* it approves the Router for the output owed to the maker;
* it pays the exact MEV tax owed, from its ETH balance, so `fill` needs no `msg.value`.
  Keep enough ETH in the contract for the tax (send it with `fill`, or fund it beforehand).
  Surplus and refunds stay in the contract; `withdraw` sends them to the owner.

## Constants

### POOLMANAGER

```solidity
IPoolManager public immutable POOLMANAGER;
```

### ROUTER

```solidity
IAsyncSwapCallback public immutable ROUTER;
```

### OWNER

```solidity
address public immutable OWNER;
```

## Functions

<a id="constructor-ipoolmanager-iasyncswapcallback-address" />


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| poolManager | `IPoolManager` |  |
| router | `IAsyncSwapCallback` |  |
| owner | `address` |  |

<a id="fill-asyncorder-uint256-bytes" />

### fill

Starts a flash fill of `order`. Any ETH sent stays here to pay the MEV tax.

```solidity
function fill(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata data) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `uint256` |  |

<a id="asyncswapflashfill-asyncorder-uint256-uint256-bytes" />

### asyncSwapFlashFill

Called by the Router inside its PoolManager unlock, after the order was closed and its input,
less the 0.02% trade fee, credited to the filler as ERC-6909 claims (`amountIn` of the input
currency, id 0 for native ETH).

<i>
  Before returning, the filler must hold `amountOwed` claims of the order's output currency and allow
  the Router to transfer them (`PoolManager.approve(router, id, amountOwed)` or an operator grant). Inside
  the callback it may swap on any v4 pool, `burn`/`mint`/`take`/`settle`, and fill other Async Swap orders
  through `IAsyncSwapCallback.fillOrderInCallback` and `matchBookInCallback`. Every delta it opens must be zero
  when the Router's unlock ends.
</i>

```solidity
function asyncSwapFlashFill(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOwed, bytes calldata data)
        external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOwed | `uint256` |  |
| data | `bytes` |  |

<a id="withdraw-uint256-uint256-uint256" />

### withdraw


**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

| amounts | `uint256[]` |  |

<a id="_route-asyncorder-uint256-uint256-bytes" />

### \_route

<i>
  Turn `amountIn` input claims into at least `amountOwed` output claims held by this contract. Runs inside
  the PoolManager unlock: swap on v4 pools, call `ROUTER.fillOrderInCallback` or `matchBookInCallback`.
  Every delta this contract opens must be zero when it returns.
</i>

```solidity
function _route(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOwed, bytes calldata data)
        internal
        virtual;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOwed | `uint256` |  |
| data | `bytes` |  |

# AsyncOrderLibrary

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/types/AsyncOrder.sol)

**Title:** AsyncOrderLibrary

Helpers attached to AsyncOrder for identity and pricing.

## Functions

<a id="orderid-asyncorder" />

### orderId

Stable identifier for an order, derived from its addressing fields.

<i>
  (chainId, poolId, owner, zeroForOne, salt) uniquely identifies one open order.

  * `block.chainid` keeps ids unique across chains where the same PoolKey can be
    deployed (for example Unichain mainnet and Sepolia).
  * `salt` is contract-assigned at create time and stored off-chain (in the event
    log) so the maker can pass it back when calling cancel / updatePrice / fill.
    `view` (not `pure`) because `block.chainid` reads EVM context.
</i>

```solidity
function orderId(AsyncOrder calldata order) internal view returns (bytes32);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes32` |  |

# AsyncOrder

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/db503f7f95d5ccf59d6e7fcbb0e4507dab24c838/src/types/AsyncOrder.sol)

Represents an async order for a swap in the Uniswap V4 pool.

```solidity
struct AsyncOrder {
    PoolKey key;
    address owner;
    bool zeroForOne;
    uint256 amountIn;
    uint256 amountOutMin;
    uint256 priorityFee;
    uint160 sqrtPrice;
    bytes32 salt;
}
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| key | `PoolKey` | The Uniswap V4 PoolKey identifying the pool the order is placed against. |
| owner | `address` | The maker who supplied `amountIn` of the input currency at order submission. |
| zeroForOne | `bool` | Direction of the order. true => input is currency0, output is currency1. |
| amountIn | `uint256` | Amount of input currency the maker escrowed. Direct matching may partially fill it;<br />unused input is returned when the maker's minimum output is satisfied. |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` | Minimum amount of output currency the maker accepts. The implicit limit price is<br />`amountOutMin / amountIn`. A filler or direct match must satisfy the live minimum<br />for the amount it consumes. |
| priorityFee | `uint256` | Optional non-refundable USDC bid for equal-price priority. Zero is valid; a nonzero<br />bid must be at least $0.10, or 0.1% of the order's USDC notional when that is less.<br />Matched portions, and the remainder on a<br />fill, cancel or dust closure, go to the protocol FeeVault. |
| sqrtPrice | `uint160` | Sqrt-price limit passed to `PoolManager.swap` on submission. The hook consumes<br />the whole input in `beforeSwap`, so the pool never trades against it. |
| salt | `bytes32` | Contract-assigned salt that disambiguates orders. The hook computes this at create<br />time from `keccak256(timestamp, block.number, msg.sender, owner, amountIn,<br/>amountOutMin, priorityFee)` and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated` so the maker can reference the<br />order in cancel / updatePrice. Submitters pass `bytes32(0)` on create — the value<br />in this slot is only read on cancel / updatePrice / fill paths. |
